title: Get started
text:
Memora

Second brain for your AI.
Long-term memory for AI agents, on your own server.

Website · Documentation · Quick start · npm · Releases

npm install -g @codrihub/memora

Memora is a self-hosted memory vault for AI agents. Notes are plain markdown files in a git-backed folder. Agents read and write them over the Model Context Protocol (MCP); you browse, edit and govern them in a web UI. One Rust binary serves the HTTP API, the MCP endpoint, the web UI and realtime updates on a single port, with all server state in one embedded SQLite database. ## Screenshots ![Overview](docs/screenshots/overview.jpg) | | | |---|---| | ![Brain](docs/screenshots/brain.jpg) **Brain**: every folder is a region, every note a node | ![Node card](docs/screenshots/brain-node.jpg) **Node card**: links, backlinks and a preview | | ![Graph](docs/screenshots/graph.jpg) **Graph**: force, radial or cluster layouts | ![Canvas](docs/screenshots/canvas.jpg) **Canvas**: one frame per folder | | ![Reader](docs/screenshots/reader.jpg) **Reader** with contents and reading settings | ![Activity](docs/screenshots/activity.jpg) **Activity**: every agent call, live | | ![Agents](docs/screenshots/agents.jpg) **Agents & API keys**: one key per agent, scoped | ![Mnemo](docs/screenshots/mnemo.jpg) **Mnemo**: the notes agent, with its steps and the notes it used | Screenshots use a demo vault. ## Features - **Markdown you own.** Every note is a `.md` file with optional frontmatter and `[[wikilinks]]`. Edit it with any tool; nothing is locked in a database. - **Git history.** Changes are committed, so any revision can be listed, diffed and restored (`get_history`, `diff`, `restore_memory`). - **MCP for agents.** 77 tools for notes, folders, search, tags, graph traversal, history, locks, activity, pins and import/export, plus admin tools, over the streamable HTTP transport. - **Mnemo, a built-in notes agent.** Chat with your notes in the browser or the console using your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible API key. Mnemo finds, writes, tags, links, moves and tidies notes with Memora's own tools, shows every step, and has no web, shell or delete-for-good access. - **Images beside notes.** Paste or drop PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF into a note; the file lives in the note's folder and moves, goes to the Trash and comes back with it. Folder galleries show which note and section uses each image. - **API keys or OAuth.** Give each agent its own key, or let MCP clients such as Claude or ChatGPT connect with OAuth after you approve them in the browser. - **Per-agent control.** Scopes (`mcp`, `read`, `write`, `admin`), per-key tool lists, server-wide tool switches, and privacy rules that hide notes or folders from chosen agents. - **Web UI.** Brain and graph views, a canvas, the vault editor with nine reading colours, fonts and sizes, tags, live agent activity, keys, tools, access rules and settings. Installable as a PWA. - **Safe first run.** An unclaimed instance cannot be taken over by whoever finds the port: the operator console opens a short setup window and you finish in the browser. - **One port, one process.** HTTP API, MCP, UI and WebSocket share port 8400. The database has no network port. ## Quick start Three steps, about two minutes. **1. Install** (pick one, in this order of ease) ```bash # npm (Linux x86_64 / arm64, Windows x64; Node.js 22 or newer): install, then keep it running npm install -g @codrihub/memora && memora # Docker (any OS with Docker) docker run -d --name memora --restart unless-stopped -p 8400:8400 \ -v memora-data:/data -v memora-state:/state ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:latest # Native installer (Linux server with systemd, x86_64 or aarch64) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Codrihub/memora/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh ``` On Windows, install Node.js 22 or newer and use npm (see [npm](#npm-linux-x86_64--arm64-windows-x64)). **2. Get a one-time setup code** ```bash memora-cli setup --minutes 15 # npm, in a second terminal docker exec -it memora memora-cli setup --minutes 15 # Docker sudo memora-cli setup --minutes 15 # native ``` **3. Open the link it prints** (`http://:8400/login`), enter the code and create your account. Memora then asks which folder to use as the vault and shows how to connect your first agent. That is all. The sections below cover every other option. ### npm (Linux x86_64 / arm64, Windows x64) ```bash npm install -g @codrihub/memora mkdir -p ~/memora && cd ~/memora MEMORA_VAULT=./vault MEMORA_STATE=./state memora # in a second terminal, same folder: MEMORA_STATE=./state memora-cli setup --minutes 15 ``` On Windows (PowerShell): ```powershell npm install -g @codrihub/memora mkdir ~\memora; cd ~\memora $env:MEMORA_VAULT = '.\vault'; $env:MEMORA_STATE = '.\state'; memora # in a second terminal, same folder: $env:MEMORA_STATE = '.\state'; memora-cli setup --minutes 15 ``` The package carries the prebuilt release binaries and the web UI (no install script, nothing downloaded at install time) and needs Node.js 22 or newer. It is handy for trying Memora or running it under your own user; for a server, the native installer adds the systemd service. On macOS use Docker or build from source. Update with `npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest`. ### Docker (any OS) One container, notes and state in named volumes (no clone, no folder permissions): ```bash docker run -d --name memora --restart unless-stopped -p 8400:8400 \ -v memora-data:/data -v memora-state:/state ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:latest docker exec -it memora memora-cli setup --minutes 15 ``` With Docker Compose from the repository instead: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Codrihub/memora.git && cd memora cp .env.example .env # optional, every value has a default mkdir -p data state && sudo chown -R 1000:1000 data state docker compose up -d docker compose exec -it gateway memora-cli setup --minutes 15 ``` The image is `ghcr.io/codrihub/memora` (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64). See [docker/README.md](docker/README.md) for volumes, upgrades and local builds. ### Native installer (Linux x86_64 / aarch64 with systemd) One command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Codrihub/memora/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh ``` Or download it and read it first: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Codrihub/memora/main/scripts/install.sh -o install.sh less install.sh # read it first sudo sh install.sh # add --behind-proxy for a local reverse proxy sudo memora-cli # then type /web ``` The installer downloads the release for your CPU, verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS`, creates a `memora` system user, and installs a hardened `memora.service` unit. Data lives in `/var/lib/memora`. Run `sh install.sh --help` for every option, and see [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) for details. ### From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/Codrihub/memora.git && cd memora cargo build --release MEMORA_VAULT=./data MEMORA_STATE=./state ./target/release/memora # in a second terminal: ./target/release/memora-cli # then type /web ``` The server binds to `127.0.0.1:8400` by default. To install your build as a service: `sudo ./scripts/install.sh --from-source`. The web UI is built from `web/` (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)). ### First run 1. Run `memora-cli setup` (or type `/web` in the `memora-cli` console). It prints a one-time setup code and the link to open. 2. Open `http://:8400/login`, enter the code and create the owner account. 3. Choose the vault folder (`/var/lib/memora/vault` natively, `/data` in Docker). 4. Add an agent: Agents, then New agent. Pick the app and paste the config it shows. One agent per app or device. If a setup code expires unused, nothing breaks: run `memora-cli setup` again for a new code. ## Configuration Settings come from the environment (systemd unit, `.env` for Docker) and can be overridden in the state database with `memora-cli` -> `/config`; a stored value wins until you clear it. The most common ones: | Name | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `MEMORA_PORT` | `8400` | HTTP port for API, MCP, UI and WebSocket | | `MEMORA_BIND` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address (`0.0.0.0` in the container) | | `MEMORA_STATE` | `state` | Directory holding `memora.db` | | `MEMORA_VAULT` | empty | Suggested vault folder; the vault is confirmed in the browser | | `MEMORA_BASE_URL` | empty | Public URL behind a reverse proxy | | `MEMORA_DOMAIN` | empty (any) | Allowed hostnames; other hosts get 404 | | `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | empty | Remote proxies whose forwarding headers are trusted | | `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD[_FILE]`, `MEMORA_API_KEY[_FILE]` | unset | Provision an owner or an agent key at startup; only hashes are stored | | `RUST_LOG` | `info` | Log filter | The full list, precedence rules and the Docker Compose variables are in [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md). For TLS, reverse proxies and hardening, see [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). ## Connecting agents over MCP The MCP endpoint is `/mcp` on the same port. Authenticate with an API key in `Authorization: Bearer ` (or `X-API-Key`), or let the client use OAuth. Claude Code: ```bash claude mcp add --transport http memora https://memory.example.com/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer memora_live_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY" ``` Clients with an `mcpServers` JSON config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "memora": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:8400/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer memora_live_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY" } } } } ``` Clients that support MCP authorization can connect with only the URL; you approve them in the browser and they appear as keys you can restrict or revoke. The discovery card is at `/.well-known/mcp.json` and a readable tool catalog at `/tools`. [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md) covers OAuth, other clients, every tool and the error codes; [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) lists the HTTP API. ## Operating ```bash sudo systemctl status memora # native service sudo journalctl -u memora -f # logs sudo memora-cli # console: /status, /keys, /tools, /config, /backup ... sudo memora-cli db backup # consistent copy of memora.db, safe while running sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --upgrade docker compose pull && docker compose up -d # Docker upgrade ``` Back up the vault folder and `memora.db` (with `memora-cli db backup`, never a plain `cp` of the live file). See [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md#backups). ### Start, stop and restart ```bash memora-cli start # or /start in the console memora-cli stop # or /shutdown memora-cli restart # or /restart memora-cli uninstall # or /uninstall ``` They work out how this install runs: a systemd service is driven with `systemctl`, an npm or source install runs in the background (pid and log in the state folder), and inside Docker the console prints the host commands (`docker start / stop / restart memora`). Uninstall asks, with a checklist, whether to also delete your settings and your vault; both are kept unless you tick them. Details: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md#uninstall-with-memora-cli). ### Update, uninstall, troubleshooting `memora-cli update` prints the right steps for your install (npm: `npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest`, then `memora-cli restart`). Check your version with `memora --version`. Per install method, and for older versions without `memora-cli uninstall` (before 1.3.2), see [Update](docs/INSTALL.md#update), [Uninstall by hand](docs/INSTALL.md#uninstall-by-hand-versions-before-132) and [Troubleshooting](docs/INSTALL.md#troubleshooting). The owner can also **shut the server down from the browser**: Settings, Server, Shut down. Every browser and agent is disconnected until it is started again on the server. When a supervisor restarts it on its own (systemd `Restart=always`, Docker `--restart unless-stopped`), the confirmation says so and shows the stop command to use instead. ## Security notes - The owner password is hashed with argon2id. API keys (`memora_live_...`) and session ids are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; a key is shown once. - Session cookies are `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`, cookie writes are checked against the request origin, and pages use a nonce-based Content-Security-Policy. - Login and setup are rate limited with per-IP cooldowns; many failures from many IPs only slow sign-ins down and never lock the owner out. - Forwarding headers are trusted only from loopback and `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES`. - Access rules can allow or block by IP, range, CIDR and domain; loopback always stays allowed so you cannot lock yourself out. - Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy before exposing Memora to the internet. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | Document | Contents | |---|---| | [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) | Native installer, Docker, npm, updates, uninstall, troubleshooting, reverse proxy, backups | | [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) | Every setting and where it lives | | [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) | Production deployment and hardening | | [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md) | Connecting agents, OAuth, tool reference | | [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) | HTTP API | | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Crates, request flow, vault files | | [docs/DATABASE.md](docs/DATABASE.md) | State database schema | ## Project layout ``` crates/core vault: markdown, wikilinks, search, graph, git history crates/state SQLite state database (memora.db) crates/gateway password and key hashing, access checks, environment provisioning crates/mcp MCP server: tool catalog, permissions, privacy crates/http axum server: middleware, API, OAuth, UI assets (binary: memora) crates/cli operator console (binary: memora-cli) web/ web UI (TypeScript), built into crates/http/assets docker/ container entrypoint and release Dockerfile docs/ user and operator documentation scripts/ installer and maintenance scripts ``` ## Versioning Memora follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). Each release is a `vX.Y.Z` tag with a [GitHub Release](https://github.com/Codrihub/memora/releases) (static Linux binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 plus `SHA256SUMS`), npm packages for Linux and Windows, and a multi-arch image `ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:X.Y.Z`. Changes are listed in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before opening a pull request. ## License Memora is free software under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later](LICENSE). You may use, modify and share it, including commercially. If you distribute a modified version, or run one as a service for others, you must publish its source under the same license and keep the attribution in [NOTICE](NOTICE): "Based on Memora by Codrihub Tech". The name and logo are covered by [TRADEMARK.md](TRADEMARK.md). Versions 1.3.8 and earlier were released under the MIT License.

title: Install
text:
# Installing Memora

Memora ships as two binaries plus a folder of web UI assets:

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `memora` | The server: HTTP API, MCP, web UI, and WebSocket on **one TCP port** (default `8400`) |
| `memora-cli` | The operator console. Run it with no arguments for slash commands (`/guide`, `/web`, `/config`, ...) |
| `assets/` | Web UI files, found through `MEMORA_ASSETS` |

It runs on Linux (x86_64, aarch64) and Windows 10/11 (x64). Install it with
**npm** (Linux and Windows, runs as you), **Docker**, the **native** installer
(a systemd service on Linux) or from source. On Windows, use npm. All end the
same way: run `memora-cli setup`, open the link it prints and enter the code.

**Fastest path** (pick one, in this order of ease), then open the link the
setup command prints and enter the code:

```bash
# npm (Linux x86_64 / arm64, Windows x64; Node.js 22 or newer)
npm install -g @codrihub/memora && memora
memora-cli setup --minutes 15            # in a second terminal

# Docker: no clone or folder permissions needed (named volumes)
docker run -d --name memora --restart unless-stopped -p 8400:8400 \
  -v memora-data:/data -v memora-state:/state ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:latest
docker exec -it memora memora-cli setup --minutes 15

# Native installer (Linux server with systemd)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Codrihub/memora/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh
sudo memora-cli setup --minutes 15
```

- [Native install](#native-install)

## Network exposure

Memora opens exactly **one TCP port**. The HTTP API, MCP (`/mcp`), the web UI,
and the realtime WebSocket (`/ws`) all share it. The local event intake
`/_bus` answers on the same port but only to loopback clients.

The state database is embedded SQLite (`<state>/memora.db`). The server creates
and migrates it on first start; it opens no port and needs no separate
database server or install.

Nothing else listens. Allow only that one port through the firewall, or none at
all when a reverse proxy on the same host is the entry point
(`--behind-proxy`).

## Native install

Requirements: Linux on x86_64 or aarch64 with systemd, `curl` (or `wget`),
`tar`, `sha256sum`, and `git` (vault history uses it).

```sh
# Inspect first: https://github.com/Codrihub/memora/blob/main/scripts/install.sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Codrihub/memora/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh
```

Pass flags after `sh -s --`, for example:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Codrihub/memora/main/scripts/install.sh \
  | sudo sh -s -- --version 1.0.0 --behind-proxy
```

or download the script and run it: `sudo sh install.sh --help`.

The script is idempotent: running it again reinstalls the same files and keeps
the port and bind address of the existing unit unless you pass new ones.

### What it does

1. Downloads `memora-<version>-<arch>-linux.tar.gz` for this CPU from GitHub
   Releases (the latest, or `--version`), downloads `SHA256SUMS` from the same
   release, and refuses to continue if the checksum does not match.
2. Installs the binaries atomically (copy to a temp file, then `mv`).
3. Creates the system user and group `memora` (no login shell, home
   `/var/lib/memora`).
4. Creates `/var/lib/memora/state` (`0700`) and `/var/lib/memora/vault`
   (`0750`), owned by `memora`.
5. Writes `/etc/systemd/system/memora.service`, enables and starts it, waits
   for `/healthz`, then verifies the state database with `memora-cli db check`.
6. Prints the next step and, when listening on every interface, a firewall
   hint.

### Paths

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `/usr/local/bin/memora`, `/usr/local/bin/memora-cli` | Binaries |
| `/usr/local/share/memora/assets/` | Web UI |
| `/usr/local/share/memora/VERSION` | Installed version (read by `--check`) |
| `/usr/local/share/memora/install.sh` | Copy of the installer, used for `--upgrade`, `--check`, `--uninstall`, and `memora-cli update` |
| `/var/lib/memora/state/` | `memora.db` (owner, API key hashes, sessions, settings, activity log), `backups/` |
| `/var/lib/memora/vault/` | Suggested vault folder (chosen in the browser after the first sign-in) |
| `/etc/systemd/system/memora.service` | The unit |

`--prefix` moves the first four (default `/usr/local`), `--data-dir` moves the
last two (default `/var/lib/memora`).

### Flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | Install or reinstall the latest release |
| `--version X.Y.Z` | Install that release |
| `--from-source` | Build with `cargo build --release --locked` in the checkout the script lives in (`sudo ./scripts/install.sh --from-source`); built as `$SUDO_USER` |
| `--from-dir PATH` | Install `PATH/memora`, `PATH/memora-cli`, `PATH/assets/` (an unpacked release, or your own build). Version from `--version`, else `PATH/VERSION` |
| `--port N` | Port (default `8400`) |
| `--bind ADDR` | Bind address (default `0.0.0.0`) |
| `--behind-proxy` | Bind `127.0.0.1`; a reverse proxy on this host is the only entry |
| `--prefix DIR` | Install prefix (default `/usr/local`) |
| `--data-dir DIR` | Data root (default `/var/lib/memora`) |
| `--no-start` | Install and enable, but do not start |
| `--no-systemd` | Skip the unit and the system user (containers, tests); prints the command to start the server by hand |
| `--upgrade` | Replace binaries and assets, keep state, restart the service if it was running |
| `--force` | With `--upgrade`: reinstall even when already up to date |
| `--uninstall` | Stop and remove the unit, binaries, and assets; keep data |
| `--purge` | With `--uninstall`: also delete the data dir and the `memora` user (asks first) |
| `--check` | Print `MEMORA_LATEST=` and `MEMORA_INSTALLED=`; change nothing |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Never ask (needed for `--purge` without a terminal) |
| `--dry-run` | Print every action, change nothing |
| `--repo OWNER/NAME` | Download from another GitHub repository (forks); also settable as `MEMORA_REPO` |

`MEMORA_RELEASES_URL` points the installer at a mirror that serves the same
layout as GitHub (`<url>/latest`, `<url>/download/vX.Y.Z/<file>`).

Root is required except for `--check`, `--dry-run`, and `--no-systemd` into a
prefix you can write to.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Error (see the message) |
| `2` | Bad usage |
| `3` | Already up to date (`--upgrade`) |
| `4` | Network or download failure |
| `5` | Checksum mismatch or missing from `SHA256SUMS` |
| `6` | Not running as root |
| `7` | Unsupported OS or CPU |

### The systemd unit

The installer writes this unit (shown with the default paths and port):

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Memora - long-term memory for AI agents (HTTP API + MCP + web UI)
Documentation=https://github.com/Codrihub/memora
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=memora
Group=memora
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/memora
Environment=HOME=/var/lib/memora
Environment=MEMORA_STATE=/var/lib/memora/state
Environment=MEMORA_ASSETS=/usr/local/share/memora/assets
Environment=MEMORA_PORT=8400
Environment=MEMORA_BIND=0.0.0.0
Environment=MEMORA_VAULT=/var/lib/memora/vault
Environment=GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Memora
Environment=GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=memora@localhost
Environment=GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Memora
Environment=GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=memora@localhost
Environment=RUST_LOG=info
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/memora
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
TimeoutStopSec=15
LimitNOFILE=65536
UMask=0027

# Hardening
NoNewPrivileges=yes
AmbientCapabilities=
CapabilityBoundingSet=
ProtectSystem=strict
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/memora
ProtectHome=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
PrivateDevices=yes
ProtectKernelTunables=yes
ProtectKernelModules=yes
ProtectKernelLogs=yes
ProtectControlGroups=yes
ProtectClock=yes
ProtectHostname=yes
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6
RestrictNamespaces=yes
RestrictRealtime=yes
RestrictSUIDSGID=yes
LockPersonality=yes
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=yes
SystemCallArchitectures=native
SystemCallFilter=@system-service
SystemCallFilter=~@privileged

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

A port below 1024 adds `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` instead of the empty capability
set. There are no IP restrictions (`IPAddressDeny=`) by default; use the
firewall, `MEMORA_DOMAIN`, or the access rules in the UI.

The installer rewrites the unit on every run. Put local changes in a drop-in:

```sh
sudo systemctl edit memora     # for example, a vault outside /var/lib/memora:
#   [Service]
#   ReadWritePaths=/srv/notes
sudo systemctl restart memora
```

Because of `ProtectSystem=strict` and `ProtectHome=yes`, the server can only
write under `/var/lib/memora`. A vault anywhere else (including `/home`) needs
the drop-in above (and `ProtectHome=read-only` or `no` for `/home`).

### Settings

The unit sets the basics (`MEMORA_STATE`, `MEMORA_ASSETS`, `MEMORA_PORT`,
`MEMORA_BIND`, `MEMORA_VAULT`, `RUST_LOG`) as `Environment=` lines. Everything
else (`MEMORA_BASE_URL`, `MEMORA_DOMAIN`, `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, ...) is
stored in the state database (table `server_config`). Edit it with the
console: `sudo memora-cli` → `/config`, then `/restart`.

A value stored with `/config` wins over the unit's `Environment=` lines; a key
with no stored value uses the environment. If you stored `MEMORA_PORT` with
`/config` and later reinstall with `--port`, change or clear it in `/config`
too, otherwise the stored value keeps applying. The provisioning owner
password and API key are environment-only and never stored (see
[CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md)).

See [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md) for every variable.

### First run

```sh
sudo memora-cli        # opens the console; it finds the running server itself
/guide                 # step-by-step, or:
/web                   # prints a one-time code
```

Open `http://<host>:8400/login`, enter the code, create the owner account, then
choose the vault folder (`/var/lib/memora/vault` is suggested).

### Day to day

```sh
sudo systemctl status memora
sudo systemctl restart memora
sudo journalctl -u memora -f
sudo memora-cli                 # /status, /keys, /config, /restart, /mcp ...
```

### Upgrading

```sh
sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --upgrade            # latest release
sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --upgrade --version 1.0.1
sudo memora-cli update                                       # same, from the console
```

Binaries and assets are swapped atomically, the state directory and vault are
untouched, and the service is restarted if it was running. The server migrates
`memora.db` itself on start. Take a `memora-cli db backup` before upgrading,
and read the [CHANGELOG](../CHANGELOG.md) before a major version bump.

### Uninstall

```sh
sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --uninstall           # keeps /var/lib/memora and the memora user
sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --uninstall --purge   # also deletes notes, account, keys, and the user
```

Or run `memora-cli uninstall`, which asks what to keep (see
[Uninstall with memora-cli](#uninstall-with-memora-cli)).

### Firewall

Open only the Memora port, and only when clients connect directly:

```sh
sudo ufw allow 8400/tcp
# or
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8400/tcp && sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

Behind a reverse proxy on the same host, install with `--behind-proxy` and open
only the proxy's 80/443.

## Docker

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Codrihub/memora.git && cd memora
mkdir -p data state && sudo chown -R 1000:1000 data state
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec -it gateway memora-cli      # then /guide, or /web
```

`docker compose up` pulls `ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:<version>`; if the image is
not available (or you set `IMAGE=memora:local`) it builds from the
`Dockerfile`. Image tags: `<version>` (for example `1.0.0`), `<major>.<minor>`
(for example `1.0`), and `latest` (stable releases only), for `linux/amd64`
and `linux/arm64`. The compose file pins the release it ships with; set
`IMAGE` in `.env` to run another tag.

### Volumes: `/data` and `/state`

Both must be persistent (the Compose file bind-mounts `./data` and `./state`):

- `/data` is the vault: your notes, their git history, and the event
  log. Lose it and the notes are gone.
- `/state` holds `memora.db` (owner account, password hash, API key hashes,
  sessions, settings, setup/lock state, activity log). Lose it and
  every agent key stops working, the instance falls back to first-run setup,
  and anyone who reaches the port during that window could claim it.

The container runs as uid 1000; set `MEMORA_UID`/`MEMORA_GID` in `.env` if the
host directories belong to another user. `MEMORA_DATA_DIR` and
`MEMORA_STATE_DIR` move the host directories, and `MEMORA_HTTP_PORT` changes
the published host port. See [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md#docker-compose-env).

### Verify

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8400/healthz
docker compose exec gateway memora-cli db check
docker compose exec gateway memora-cli status
ls -l state/memora.db
```

### Upgrading

```sh
git pull
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d     # or: docker compose up -d --build
```

Settings: `docker compose exec -it gateway memora-cli` → `/config`, then
`docker compose restart gateway` (`/restart` cannot restart a container from
inside).

## npm

Requirements: Linux on x86_64 or arm64, or Windows 10/11 on x64; Node.js 22 or
newer; and `git` (vault history uses it).

```sh
npm install -g @codrihub/memora
mkdir -p ~/memora && cd ~/memora
MEMORA_VAULT=./vault MEMORA_STATE=./state memora
# in a second terminal, same folder:
MEMORA_STATE=./state memora-cli                 # then /guide, or /web
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
npm install -g @codrihub/memora
mkdir ~\memora; cd ~\memora
$env:MEMORA_VAULT = '.\vault'; $env:MEMORA_STATE = '.\state'; memora
# in a second terminal, same folder:
$env:MEMORA_STATE = '.\state'; memora-cli       # then /guide, or /web
```

`npx @codrihub/memora --version` runs it without a global install.

`@codrihub/memora` holds the `memora` and `memora-cli` commands and the web UI
(used unless `MEMORA_ASSETS` is set). The binaries come from
`@codrihub/memora-linux-x64`, `@codrihub/memora-linux-arm64` or
`@codrihub/memora-win32-x64`, optional dependencies npm installs only on a
matching machine. The Linux ones are the static binaries of the GitHub
release with the same version, so glibc and musl distributions both work; the
Windows one is built with a static C runtime and needs nothing else. There is
no install script and nothing is downloaded at install time, so it works with
`--ignore-scripts` and from a registry mirror; it does not work with
`--omit=optional`, which leaves the binaries out. On macOS the commands print
where to go instead: use [Docker](#docker) or build from source.

The npm install sets up no service, user or data folder: the server runs as
you, with `MEMORA_STATE` and `MEMORA_VAULT` where you point them (`./state`
by default). Keep the state folder private (`chmod 700 state`; on Windows,
keep it under your user profile), since it holds the owner account and key
hashes. On Windows, `memora-cli` runs every command as you: there is no root
or service account to switch to. For a long-running server, prefer the
[native install](#native-install).

Upgrade with `npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest` (`memora-cli update`
prints this too) and restart the server; the state database is migrated on
start.

## Start, stop and restart

`memora-cli start`, `stop` and `restart` (or `/start`, `/shutdown` and
`/restart` in the console) work out how this install runs and do the right
thing:

| Install | What `memora-cli start / stop / restart` does | By hand |
|---|---|---|
| Native (systemd) | runs `systemctl start / stop / restart memora` (as root) | `sudo systemctl start memora` |
| npm, source | runs the server in the background, with `memora.pid`, `memora.log` and `stop.token` in the state folder; `stop` asks it to end over a local, token-protected request and waits, `stop --force` kills it | run `memora` and keep it open; Ctrl+C stops it |
| Docker | prints the host commands (a container cannot stop itself) | `docker start / stop / restart memora` |

From the browser, the owner can shut the server down in Settings, Server, Shut
down: the server answers, then stops gracefully and exits with status 0, the
same as Ctrl+C or `systemctl stop`. A supervisor that restarts a cleanly exited
process starts it again (systemd `Restart=always`, Docker
`--restart unless-stopped`); the installer's unit uses `Restart=on-failure`, so
it stays stopped. API keys cannot shut the server down.

## Update

Check what you run first: `memora --version` and `memora-cli --version`.
`memora-cli update` (or `/update` in the console) works out how this copy was
installed and prints, or runs, the right steps. By install method:

| Install | Update with | Then |
|---|---|---|
| npm (Windows, Linux) | `npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest` | `memora-cli restart`, or Ctrl+C the running `memora` and start it again |
| Docker Compose | `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` | nothing: the container is re-created |
| Docker run | `docker pull ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:latest`, then `docker rm -f memora` and the same `docker run` again (same volumes) | nothing |
| Native (systemd) | `sudo memora-cli update` (runs `install.sh --upgrade`) | nothing: the service is restarted |
| Source | `git pull && cargo build --release` | `memora-cli restart` |

Settings, accounts and notes stay; the server migrates `memora.db` on start.
Take a `memora-cli db backup` first if you are unsure.

**Release zip (older Windows installs).** Windows now installs with npm. To
switch, stop the old server (Ctrl+C in its window), run
`npm install -g @codrihub/memora`, and start `memora` with the same folders so
everything carries over, for example in PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:MEMORA_STATE = 'C:\Users\you\memora\state'; $env:MEMORA_VAULT = 'C:\Users\you\memora\vault'; memora
```

Then delete the old program folder (only the `.exe` files and `assets`, not
your state or vault folders).

## Uninstall with memora-cli

```bash
memora-cli uninstall                 # or /uninstall in the console
```

It explains what it removes for this install (the service and program
files, or the npm package, or the container), then shows a checklist; press
space to select and Enter to continue:

- **Settings and accounts** (the state folder: database, keys, sessions)
- **Vault notes** (your vault folder)

Both are **unticked**, so by default your settings and notes are kept and a
later install picks them up again. Deleting the vault asks you to type its
folder name. Before the state folder is deleted, a final database backup is
offered. System folders, your home folder and the program's own folder are
never deleted.

| Install | What uninstall does |
|---|---|
| Native (systemd) | runs the installed `install.sh --uninstall` (adds `--purge` only when both folders are the installer's own) |
| npm | stops the server, deletes what you ticked, then tells you to run `npm uninstall -g @codrihub/memora` |
| Source | stops the server, deletes what you ticked; delete the program folder yourself |
| Docker | prints `docker rm -f memora` and, for what you ticked, `docker volume rm memora-state` / `docker volume rm memora-data` |

Without a terminal it needs `--yes` and deletes only what the flags say:
`memora-cli uninstall --yes [--delete-config] [--delete-vault]`.

On a version older than 1.3.2 there is no `uninstall` command: see
[Uninstall by hand](#uninstall-by-hand-versions-before-132).

## Uninstall by hand (versions before 1.3.2)

`memora-cli uninstall` arrived in 1.3.2. On an older version it answers
``unknown command `uninstall` ``. Either update first and then run
`memora-cli uninstall` (npm: `npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest`), or
remove Memora by hand with the steps below. They only touch Memora: never use
wildcards, and never delete a parent folder or your home folder.

**1. Check the version.** `memora --version` and `memora-cli --version`.

**2. Find the folders.** Memora keeps two folders:

- the **state folder** (settings, accounts, keys): `MEMORA_STATE`, or by
  default `state` inside the folder where you started `memora` (for example
  `C:\Users\you\state` or `~/memora/state`);
- the **vault folder**: your notes, wherever you chose.

The server prints both when it starts:
`Memora HTTP server starting vault=... state=...`. `memora-cli status`, run in
the same folder, shows the state folder too.

**3. Stop Memora.** Press Ctrl+C in the window where `memora` runs (or close
that window). Then make sure it is gone:

| Shell | Check | Stop if still running |
|---|---|---|
| PowerShell | `Get-Process memora -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` | `Stop-Process -Name memora` |
| cmd | `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq memora.exe"` | `taskkill /IM memora.exe` |
| Linux, macOS | `pgrep -ax memora` | `pkill -x memora` |

**4. Remove the program.**

| Install | Commands |
|---|---|
| npm (any OS) | `npm uninstall -g @codrihub/memora`, then `npm ls -g --depth=0`: if `@codrihub/memora-win32-x64` (or `-linux-x64`, `-linux-arm64`) is still listed, `npm uninstall -g` that exact name |
| Docker run | `docker rm -f memora`, then `docker image rm ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:latest` |
| Docker Compose | `docker compose down` in the folder of `docker-compose.yml` (no `-v`) |
| Native (systemd) | `sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --uninstall` (keeps `/var/lib/memora`) |
| Release zip | delete the folder that holds `memora.exe`, `memora-cli.exe` and `assets` (check its contents first, as below) |

**5. Delete the state folder (optional).** Look inside first: it should hold
`memora.db` (and maybe `memora.log`, `memora.pid`, `stop.token`, `backups`).
Then delete that exact path:

```powershell
# Windows, PowerShell
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\you\state'
Remove-Item -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\you\state' -Recurse -Confirm
```

```bat
:: Windows, cmd
dir "C:\Users\you\state"
rmdir /S "C:\Users\you\state"
```

```sh
# Linux, macOS
ls -la ~/memora/state
rm -rI -- ~/memora/state
```

Docker: `docker volume ls`, then remove the exact names,
`docker volume rm memora-state`. Compose: check and delete the `./state`
folder next to `docker-compose.yml`. Native: `/var/lib/memora/state`
(or `install.sh --uninstall --purge`, which also deletes the notes, see below).

**6. The vault folder: only if you are sure.** It holds your notes. It is
optional to delete it; copy it somewhere safe first (it is plain Markdown).
Use the same two steps on its exact path: look inside (`Get-ChildItem` /
`ls`), then `Remove-Item -LiteralPath '<vault>' -Recurse -Confirm` or
`rm -rI -- <vault>`. Docker: `docker volume rm memora-data`, or the `./data`
folder with Compose. Native: `sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh
--uninstall --purge` deletes `/var/lib/memora` with the notes, the account
and the `memora` user.

## Troubleshooting

**``memora-cli: unknown command `uninstall` ``** (or `start`, `stop`,
`restart`). You run a version older than 1.3.2. Update, then run the command
again: `npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest`, then `memora-cli uninstall`.
Or remove it by hand: [Uninstall by hand](#uninstall-by-hand-versions-before-132).

**`/update` says "not installed with install.sh (built from source)" on an
npm install.** Older versions could miss an npm install. Update with npm,
`npm install -g @codrihub/memora@latest`, and restart the server; newer
versions detect npm reliably. Never run `cargo build` for an npm install.

**`/restart` says "systemctl restart" on npm or Windows.** Same cause (older
version). Stop the server with Ctrl+C in its window and run `memora` again, or
update and use `memora-cli restart`.

**Which version do I have?** `memora --version` and `memora-cli --version`.
The latest release is on
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Codrihub/memora/releases).

## Reverse proxy

Run Memora on loopback (`--behind-proxy` natively; in Docker set
`MEMORA_HTTP_PORT=127.0.0.1:8400` in `.env`) and let the proxy terminate TLS.
Then set, with `/config` or in `.env`:

| Variable | Why |
|---|---|
| `MEMORA_BASE_URL=https://memory.example.com` | Public URL; links and MCP snippets use it, and its host becomes an allowed domain |
| `MEMORA_DOMAIN=memory.example.com` | Only these hostnames are served; requests for the bare IP or other names get 404 |
| `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES=203.0.113.10` | Proxies whose forwarding headers are believed. Loopback (same-host nginx, cloudflared) is always trusted; only list remote proxies |

In Docker, a proxy on the host reaches the container through the Docker
network, so the container sees the network's gateway address (for example
`172.18.0.1`) instead of loopback. Add that address to
`MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, otherwise every request appears to come from it.

The proxy must forward `Host`, `X-Forwarded-For`, and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and
upgrade WebSockets on `/ws`. nginx and Caddy examples are in
[DEPLOYMENT.md](DEPLOYMENT.md).

## Backups

Back up **both** the state database and the vault. The database is small but
critical.

State, online (the server keeps running):

```sh
sudo memora-cli db backup                     # state/backups/memora-<UTC time>.db, keeps the newest 10
sudo memora-cli db backup --to /var/backups/memora.db
sudo memora-cli db check                      # integrity, permissions, sizes, last backup age
docker compose exec gateway memora-cli db backup   # Docker: lands in ./state/backups/
```

The copy is a consistent snapshot (`VACUUM INTO`), checked with
`integrity_check`, mode 0600. Never `cp` a live `memora.db`: recent commits sit
in `memora.db-wal`. Restore with the server stopped:

```sh
sudo systemctl stop memora
sudo memora-cli db restore /var/backups/memora.db   # verifies it; keeps the replaced DB in state/backups/
sudo systemctl start memora
```

Also keep a copy of `state/key-seal.bin`, which encrypts the sealed API key
copies. Vault and state together: archive both with the server stopped:

```sh
sudo systemctl stop memora
sudo tar -C /var/lib/memora -czf memora-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz state vault
sudo systemctl start memora
```

Keep backups private: the database holds password and key hashes (never
plaintext secrets).

## Automation: `--check` and `--upgrade`

These are the contract for scripts and automation.

```sh
$ /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --check
MEMORA_LATEST=1.0.1
MEMORA_INSTALLED=1.0.0
```

`MEMORA_INSTALLED` comes from `/usr/local/share/memora/VERSION` (written by
the installer), else from `memora --version`, else `unknown` (or `none` when
nothing is installed). `MEMORA_LATEST` is `unknown` and the exit code `4` when
GitHub cannot be reached. `--check` needs no root.

```sh
$ sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --upgrade --yes [--version X.Y.Z]
...
MEMORA_UPGRADE_RESULT=ok FROM=1.0.0 TO=1.0.1
```

`--upgrade --yes` never prompts. The last line of output is always
`MEMORA_UPGRADE_RESULT=<ok|uptodate|error> FROM=<old> TO=<new>`, and the exit
code is `0` (ok), `3` (already up to date), `4` (network), `5` (checksum),
`6` (not root), or `1`/`2` for other errors.

title: Configuration

# Configuration

All server state, settings included, lives in one SQLite database,
`<MEMORA_STATE>/memora.db` (see [DATABASE.md](DATABASE.md)). Server settings are
rows in the `server_config` table, edited with `memora-cli` (`/config` in the
console). The process environment (systemd `Environment=`, Docker
`environment:`) applies to every key that has no row.

## Precedence

For each server setting:

1. a row in `server_config` (set with `/config`), else
2. the process environment (non-empty value), else
3. the built-in default.

The server reads `server_config` once at startup, before anything else, so a
change made with `/config` applies after a restart (`/restart` for a native
install, `docker compose restart gateway` in Docker). Clearing a value in
`/config` deletes the row, and the environment or default applies again.

A row wins over the environment. If you set `MEMORA_PORT` with `/config` and
later change the port in the systemd unit or `.env`, the row still applies
until you clear it.

## Server settings

| Name | Default | Where it can live | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MEMORA_PORT` | `8400` | `server_config` or env | HTTP port (API, MCP, web UI, WebSocket). 1-65535. |
| `MEMORA_BIND` | `127.0.0.1` | `server_config` or env | Bind address. `0.0.0.0` for every interface (the container image and the installer set it). |
| `MEMORA_BASE_URL` | empty | `server_config` or env | Public URL, for example `https://memory.example.com`. Used for OAuth metadata and connection snippets; its host is also an allowed domain. |
| `MEMORA_DOMAIN` | empty (any host) | `server_config` or env | Allowed hostnames, comma separated (`*.example.com` works). Requests for other hosts get 404. Loopback names are always allowed. |
| `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | empty | `server_config` or env | IPs of remote reverse proxies whose forwarding headers are trusted. Loopback is always trusted. |
| `MEMORA_ARM_TTL` | `300` | `server_config` or env | Accepted and validated (30-86400 seconds), but the server and `memora-cli` do not read it: the setup / reset window length comes from `memora-cli --minutes` (default 5 minutes). |
| `MEMORA_VAULT` | empty (`data` as last resort) | `server_config` or env | Suggested vault folder. The vault in use is chosen in the browser (or with `memora-cli vault`) and stored in the `settings` table. |
| `MEMORA_VAULT_AUTO` | `false` | `server_config` or env | `true` (also `1`, `yes`, `on`): use `MEMORA_VAULT` at startup instead of asking in the browser, only while no vault is configured and if the folder is writable. |
| `MEMORA_ADMIN_USER` | `admin` | `server_config` or env | Name of the owner created at startup when no owner exists (needs `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`). |
| `RUST_LOG` | `info` | `server_config` or env | Log filter, for example `info` or `memora=debug`. |

`server_config` accepts only these ten keys. Values are trimmed and validated
(numbers in range, `true`/`false`, a valid user name, no control characters, at
most 2048 bytes).

## Environment only

| Name | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE` | unset | Creates the owner at startup when none exists (at least 10 characters). Only the argon2id hash is stored; an existing owner is never replaced. |
| `MEMORA_API_KEY`, `MEMORA_API_KEY_FILE` | unset | Installs an agent API key with id `k_env` and scopes `mcp`, `read`, `write` (at least 24 characters). Only its SHA-256 is stored; the key is replaced when the value changes. |
| `MEMORA_STATE` | `state` (relative to the working directory) | State directory holding `memora.db`. Created with mode 0700 if missing. |
| `MEMORA_ASSETS` | the `crates/http/assets` folder of the build tree | Directory of the web UI assets. |
| `MEMORA_INSTALL` | set by the npm launcher (`npm`) and the Docker image (`docker`) | How this copy was installed: `npm`, `docker`, `native`, `zip` or `source`. `memora-cli update`, `start`, `stop`, `restart` and `uninstall` use it to pick the right steps; when unset they work it out from the program's path. |
| `MEMORA_SETUP_HINT` | `memora-cli setup (run on the server)` | Hint returned by `GET /api/auth/state` and shown on the login screen. |
| `MEMORA_UPDATE_CHECK` | `true` | Release check: shortly after start and then every 6 hours the server asks GitHub (`api.github.com/repos/Codrihub/memora/releases/latest`) for the newest release and the web UI shows when an update is available. The same check reads the repository's star count (`api.github.com/repos/Codrihub/memora`), shown in What's new. `false` (also `0`, `no`, `off`) turns both off; no network call is made. |

The two secrets can never be stored in `server_config` (the schema rejects
them). The `_FILE` variants read the value from a file, for example a Docker
secret; a non-empty file wins over the plain variable.

In `/config`, `MEMORA_API_KEY` offers to create an API key directly, and
`MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` points to `/setup` or `/reset`.

## Instance settings (web UI)

The `settings` table holds one row, edited from the Settings page of the web UI:

| Key | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `realm` | `Memora` | 1-64 characters | Instance name shown in the UI and reported by `/api/config` and `/api/auth/state`. |
| `session_ttl` | `10800` (3 hours) | 300-2592000 seconds | Idle timeout of a browser session: any use renews it (requests, and an open tab in use). |
| `session_max_age` | `0` | `0` or at least `session_ttl` | Absolute session lifetime in seconds. `0` means no cap. |
| `min_password_len` | `10` | 10-256 | Minimum owner password length. |
| `log_max_mb` | `8` | 1-512 | Size limit in MB of the vault event log (`.events.jsonl`). |
| `log_max_days` | `0` | 0-3650 | Age limit in days of the vault event log. `0` means no age limit. |
| `vault_path` | unset | absolute path | The vault folder. Set in the browser after the first sign-in, or with `memora-cli vault PATH`. |

Two more settings live in the `ui_layout` table and in a file beside the database:

| Setting | Default | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Largest image | 5 MB | Settings, Images (`POST /api/settings/media`, admin); stored as the `srv-media` document | Uploads above this size are refused, from the app, the HTTP API and MCP `upload_image` alike. 0.1 to 50 MB. |
| Mnemo | not set up | Settings, Mnemo, or `/mnemo setup` in the console; stored in `assistant.sqlite3` | Providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, one OpenAI-compatible server) with sealed API keys, models (pinned, hidden, default, context window and reply limit), temperature, reply and context limits, tool steps per reply, your instructions, and the floating button. |

## memora-cli options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--state <DIR>` | `$MEMORA_STATE`, else the state directory of the running `memora` server, else `./state` | State directory to work on. |
| `--minutes <N>` | `5` | Window length for `setup` and `reset-password`, 1-60. |
| `--ttl <SECONDS>` | | Window length in seconds (at most 3600). `--minutes` wins when both are given. |
| `--create` | | With `vault PATH`: create the folder if it does not exist. |

Run as root, `memora-cli` does all database work as the owner of the state
directory, so no root-owned `memora.db*` files appear. See
[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) and [DEPLOYMENT.md](DEPLOYMENT.md) for the commands.

## Docker Compose (`.env`)

These variables are read by `docker-compose.yml`, not by Memora itself:

| Name | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` | `memora` | Compose project name, also the container name prefix. |
| `IMAGE` | `ghcr.io/codrihub/memora:<version>` | Image to run or build. The compose file pins the release it ships with. |
| `MEMORA_HTTP_PORT` | `8400` | Host port mapped to the container's port 8400. Use `127.0.0.1:8400` to publish on loopback only. |
| `MEMORA_DATA_DIR` | `./data` | Host path mounted at `/data` (the vault). |
| `MEMORA_STATE_DIR` | `./state` | Host path mounted at `/state` (the state directory). |
| `MEMORA_UID`, `MEMORA_GID` | `1000` | uid:gid the container runs as. Must own both host directories. |
| `MEMORA_ARM_TTL` | `300` | Passed to the container unchanged. |

Compose also passes these through from `.env` to the container:
`MEMORA_BASE_URL`, `MEMORA_DOMAIN`, `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES`,
`MEMORA_VAULT_AUTO`, `MEMORA_ADMIN_USER`, `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`,
`MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE`, `MEMORA_API_KEY`, `MEMORA_API_KEY_FILE`,
`MEMORA_SETUP_HINT`, `MEMORA_UPDATE_CHECK`, and `RUST_LOG`.

Inside the container the image sets `MEMORA_VAULT=/data`,
`MEMORA_STATE=/state`, `MEMORA_PORT=8400`, `MEMORA_BIND=0.0.0.0`,
`MEMORA_ARM_TTL=300`, `MEMORA_ASSETS=/app/assets`, `MEMORA_INSTALL=docker`,
and `RUST_LOG=info`.

## State directory

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `memora.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`) | The state database: owner, API keys (hashes), tool switches and per-key permissions, OAuth clients and grants, privacy rules, sessions (hashed ids), setup window and lock state, access rules, settings, `server_config`, activity log. Mode 0600, WAL mode, must be on a local filesystem. See [DATABASE.md](DATABASE.md). |
| `key-seal.bin` | 32-byte master key (mode 0600) that encrypts the copies of dashboard-created API keys, so the owner can show a key again. Created on first use. Back it up together with `memora.db`. |
| `assistant.sqlite3` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`) | Mnemo, the built-in agent: providers (API keys sealed with `key-seal.bin`), models, preferences, chats and messages. Mode 0600. Separate from `memora.db`, so the main schema is unchanged; delete it to forget every Mnemo chat and key. Back it up with `memora.db` if you want to keep chats. |
| `backups/` | `memora-cli db backup` output (newest 10 kept by default). |
| `exchange/` | Zips written by the `export_memory` MCP tool and read by `import_memory` (mode 0700, created on first use). Private to this instance; delete old zips when no longer needed. |
| `legacy-json-<unix time>/` | JSON state files found at startup, moved here after their one-time import into `memora.db`. |
| `internal.token` | Created by the Docker entrypoint. Not used by Memora. |

## Vault files

The vault holds the markdown notes plus derived and metadata files. See
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#vault-markdown-portable) for the full list.
The important ones for operations are `.git/` (history), `.events.jsonl`
(event log), and `.Trash/`
(soft-deleted notes; `.Trash/.index.json` remembers where each one came from,
so `restore_trash` puts it back there; `.Trash/.assets/<entry>/` keeps the images
of a trashed note until it is restored or deleted for good). Images uploaded to a
note are ordinary files in the note's folder.

## Version history

Version history (`get_history`, `get_note_at`, `diff`, `restore_memory`,
`snapshot`) is on when the vault folder is a git repository of its own, that is
when it has a `.git/` directory. Memora does not create one, so a new vault has
no history and these tools answer "version history is off". To turn it on,
install `git` and run, once:

```sh
git -C /path/to/vault init
git -C /path/to/vault add -A
git -C /path/to/vault commit -m "start history"
```

(In Docker, the vault is the host directory mounted at `/data`.) From then on
every change made through Memora is committed automatically. Each commit's
author is the agent or user whose call made the change; the committer is the
vault's git identity (`git config user.name` / `user.email`), or `Memora
<memora@localhost>` when none is set. Git never searches above the vault, so a
vault inside another repository still needs its own `git init`.

A snapshot (`snapshot` tool) commits pending changes and tags the last commit
as `snap-<label>`; pass that tag as `rev` to `get_note_at`, `diff` or
`restore_memory`.

Deleting a note for good (Delete forever or Empty trash in the app,
`/api/trash/delete`, `/api/trash/empty`, `delete_memory` with `permanent`)
also erases it from the history: Memora rewrites the vault's git history so
no commit, snapshot tag or object keeps its text, any name it had, its trash
record or its path in a commit message, then expires the reflog and runs
`git gc --prune=now`. Other notes keep all their versions, but their revision
ids change, so old revision ids (and clones or pushes of the vault made
before) no longer match. Moving a note to the Trash keeps its history.
