# MCP

Memora exposes the vault to agents through the Model Context Protocol. The
server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Streamable HTTP transport at `/mcp`, on the
same port as the HTTP API and the web UI. There is one MCP endpoint and one tool
catalog.

| | |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `POST /mcp` |
| Protocol versions | `2025-06-18` (preferred), `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05` |
| Auth | API key in `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`, or an OAuth 2.1 access token |
| Discovery card | `GET /.well-known/mcp.json` (public) |
| Readable catalog | `GET /tools` (HTML page, public) |
| Catalog size | 77 tools, plus 5 admin tools for keys with the `admin` scope |

`initialize` answers with the protocol version the client asks for when it is
one of the three above, and with `2025-06-18` otherwise.

## Transport

- Requests are JSON-RPC 2.0 objects sent with `POST /mcp`. Batches (JSON
  arrays) are not supported.
- Responses are plain JSON (`application/json`), with one exception below.
- `initialize` returns an `Mcp-Session-Id` header (`<catalog epoch>.<random>`).
  The epoch is a hash of the server version and the tools the caller may use, so
  it changes when the server is upgraded, a tool is switched on or off, or the
  key's scopes or tool grant change. No session id is ever refused: unknown or
  old ids work, and malformed ones count as no session.
- When a request carries a session id whose catalog has changed since that
  session last heard, and its `Accept` header allows `text/event-stream`, the
  answer is an SSE stream with two events: the notification
  `notifications/tools/list_changed`, then the normal response. Each change is
  sent once per session (remembered in memory; a restart forgets, and the
  epoch in the id takes over). JSON-only clients always get plain JSON.
- `GET /mcp` returns `405 Method Not Allowed` (there is no standalone server
  stream). `DELETE /mcp` with a session id returns `204 No Content`; without
  one it returns `405`.
- A notification (a `notifications/*` method without an `id`) gets
  `202 Accepted` and no body.
- `/mcp` needs a configured vault. Until one is chosen it returns
  `409 {"error":"vault not configured","needs_vault":true}`.
- A browser session (cookie) may also call `/mcp`. It then needs a same-origin
  request, like the rest of the JSON API.

The server speaks Streamable HTTP only. A client that can only launch local stdio
servers can use a bridge such as `mcp-remote` (see below).

## Connecting an agent

### With an API key

Create a key in the web UI (Keys page), with `memora-cli` (`/keys`), or with
`POST /api/keys`. The raw key (`memora_live_...`) is shown once. By default a key gets
the scopes `mcp`, `read` and `write` and may call every tool. See
[Tool switches and per-key permissions](contracts/tools-permissions.md) to
narrow it.

Use `http://localhost:8400/mcp` for a local install, or your public URL such as
`https://memory.example.com/mcp` behind a reverse proxy. When the server sets
`MEMORA_DOMAIN` or `MEMORA_BASE_URL`, requests for any other host get `404`, so
use that domain.

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http memora https://memory.example.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer memora_live_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
```

Cursor, Windsurf and other clients with an `mcpServers` JSON config (VS Code
uses the key `servers` in `.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memora": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:8400/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer memora_live_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`), with the key in the `MEMORA_API_KEY`
environment variable:

```toml
[mcp_servers.memora]
url = "https://memory.example.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "MEMORA_API_KEY"
```

Clients that only run local stdio servers, such as the Claude Desktop config
file, can bridge with `mcp-remote` (needs Node.js):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memora": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://memory.example.com/mcp",
        "--header", "Authorization: Bearer memora_live_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Some clients send the key as `X-API-Key: <key>` instead. Both headers are
accepted.

### With OAuth

Clients that support MCP authorization (for example Claude and ChatGPT custom
connectors, or Claude Code without a `--header`) can connect with only the URL:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http memora https://memory.example.com/mcp
```

The flow:

1. The client calls `/mcp` without credentials and gets `401` with
   `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://memory.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`.
2. It reads the protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) and the authorization
   server metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414; also
   served at `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and under a `/mcp` suffix).
3. It registers itself with dynamic client registration at
   `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591), or uses an HTTPS client metadata document
   URL as its `client_id`. The owner can also register clients in the web UI.
   Redirect URIs must be HTTPS, or plain HTTP on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or
   `[::1]`.
4. It opens `/oauth/authorize` (authorization code with PKCE `S256` only). The
   browser lands on the Memora sign-in page, and the signed-in owner approves or
   denies the connection on a consent card. Codes are valid for 10 minutes.
5. It exchanges the code at `POST /oauth/token` and receives an access token and
   a refresh token. The only OAuth scope is `mcp`.

The access token is a regular Memora API key named after the client. It starts
with the default scopes (`mcp`, `read`, `write`) and every tool, and it shows up
on the Keys page like any other key, so you can restrict, disable or delete it
there. The access token has no expiry. A `refresh_token` grant replaces it with
a fresh one (the old token stops working at once) and rotates the refresh token.
Disabling or deleting the key ends the connection.

Set `MEMORA_BASE_URL` (for example `https://memory.example.com`) when the server
runs behind a proxy, so the issuer and endpoint URLs in the metadata are the
public ones. Without it the server derives them from the request headers.

### Test from a shell

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8400/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer memora_live_REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

## Discovery card

`GET /.well-known/mcp.json` needs no auth and returns:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `name` | `memora` |
| `version` | The server version |
| `description` | One-line description of the server |
| `mcp` | `{endpoint: "/mcp", transports: ["streamable-http"], protocolVersion: "2025-06-18"}` |
| `auth` | `{type: "api-key", headers: ["Authorization: Bearer <key>", "X-API-Key: <key>"], oauth: "/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"}` |
| `capabilities` | `{tools: true, resources: true, prompts: false}` |
| `tools` | Every catalog tool as `{name, category, description, enabled}`. `enabled` is `false` for tools switched off on this server. Admin tools are not listed. |
| `resources` | `[{uri, name}]` for the three resources below |

The card is the same for every caller. To see what a given key may call, use
`tools/list` with that key.

## Methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | Handshake. Returns `protocolVersion`, `serverInfo` (`{name, version}`) and `capabilities` (`tools` with `listChanged: true`, `resources` with `listChanged: false`). |
| `notifications/initialized` | Client notification. Without an `id` it gets `202 Accepted`. |
| `tools/list` | The tools the caller may use, each with `name`, `description` (what it does and when to use it), `inputSchema`, and `_meta.category`. |
| `tools/call` | Runs one tool. Params are `{name, arguments}`. |
| `resources/list` | Lists the three resources below. |
| `resources/read` | Reads one resource. Params are `{uri}`. |

There are no prompts and no pagination cursors. The only notification the server
sends is `notifications/tools/list_changed` (see Transport).

### Resources

| URI | Content |
|---|---|
| `memory://catalog` | Every catalog tool with `name`, `category`, `description`, `when`, and `inputSchema` (JSON) |
| `memory://schema` | Data shapes for a note, a folder, the graph, and activity (JSON) |
| `memory://guide` | A short guide for agents using the vault (Markdown) |

`resources/read` returns `{contents: [{uri, mimeType, text}]}`.

## Results and errors

A successful tool call returns the tool's JSON result as text:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{...}" }],
    "isError": false
  }
}
```

A tool that fails (bad arguments, note not found, unknown tool name) returns the
same envelope with `isError: true` and the error message as the text. The HTTP
status stays `200`.

JSON-RPC errors:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `-32700` | The body is not valid JSON (HTTP `400`). |
| `-32600` | The body is not a JSON-RPC request object (HTTP `400`). |
| `-32601` | Unknown method: `unsupported method: <method>`. |
| `-32602` | `resources/read` with an unknown URI: `unknown resource: <uri>`. |
| `-32003` | The tool exists but the caller may not use it. Messages: `tool not allowed for this API key: <name>`, `tool disabled on this server: <name>`, `API key lacks the 'write' scope for tool: <name>`. |

HTTP errors before JSON-RPC runs:

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | No key, or a key that is unknown, disabled, deleted or replaced by a roll (`invalid API key`). Carries a `WWW-Authenticate` header that points OAuth clients at the protected resource metadata. |
| `403` | The key lacks the `mcp` scope (`{"error":"API key lacks the 'mcp' scope","required_scope":"mcp"}`), or a browser request failed the same-origin check. |
| `405` | Any method other than `POST`. |
| `409` | No vault is configured yet. |
| `429` | Rate limit or cooldown after failed attempts. |

## What each key sees

`tools/list` is filtered per caller:

- A tool switched off on the server is hidden for everyone.
- A key whose tool list is not `"*"` only sees the tools in its list.
- A key without the `write` scope only sees read-only tools.
- Admin tools are added for keys with the `admin` scope (and for browser
  sessions).

`tools/call` on a tool that `tools/list` would hide returns `-32003`. Details
are in [Tool switches and per-key permissions](contracts/tools-permissions.md).

### Privacy rules

The owner can hide notes and folders from specific agents (web UI,
`/api/privacy`, or the `privacy_*` admin tools). For an API key covered by a
rule, every tool works as if the hidden paths did not exist: they are left out
of listings, search, the graph, tags, events, logs, locks and folder metadata; a
hidden path named in an argument is answered as not found, for reads and writes
alike; and folder operations that would carry hidden items along are refused.
If the rules cannot be read, the key sees nothing (fail closed). Browser
sessions are never filtered.

## Tools

R = read-only (needs only the `mcp` scope). W = changes the vault or server
state (also needs the `write` scope). Unless marked required, arguments are
optional. Paths are vault-relative, for example `Projects/Plan.md`. A path
copied in the web app (Copy path in a note or folder menu) works as is as the
`path` argument of `read_memory` and the other tools.

### Notes (`note`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_memory` | R | none | Every note grouped by its folder, the full parent path (`Projects/Atlas`; `Root` for the top level): `{folder: [{path, name, folder, mtime}]}`. |
| `read_memory` | R | `path` (string, required) | Markdown body, frontmatter, tags and backlinks of one note. A `\` in a path is read as `/`; replies echo the normalized path. |
| `create_memory` | W | `title` (string, required), `folder` (string relative to the vault, default `Memory` when omitted or empty; `Root` for the top level), `content` (string; default is a stub with `created` frontmatter and a heading) | Creates `<folder>/<title>.md` and returns `{ok, path}`. A trailing `.md` in the title is dropped; `/` and `\` in a title, an absolute folder and a folder that is a note are refused. Spaces are kept; `: * ? " < > | # ^ [ ]` and a leading dot are removed and names are cut at 80 characters; the reply then adds `renamed_from` and a `note`. A note whose name differs only in case from an existing one is refused. |
| `save_memory` | W | `path` (string, required), `content` (string, required) | Replaces the whole note. |
| `patch_memory` | W | `path` (string, required), `ops` (array, required) | Partial edits. Each op is an object: `{op:"append", text}`, `{op:"prepend", text}`, `{op:"replace", find, with}`, `{op:"set_field", field, value}`, `{op:"add_tag", tag}`, `{op:"remove_tag", tag}`. |
| `delete_memory` | W | `path` (string, required), `permanent` (boolean, default false) | Moves a note to the Trash (`.Trash`), remembering where it came from and who deleted it: `{ok, path, trashed, to}`. `list_trash` shows it and `restore_trash` brings it back. `permanent: true` deletes it for good instead (`{ok, path, permanent}`) and is refused for keys without the `admin` scope. With version history on, every earlier version is erased from the history as well (every name the note had, its trash record and the commit messages naming it; other notes keep their versions but their revision ids change), so no one, agents included, can read it again. |
| `move_memory` | W | `path` (string, required), `folder` (string, required; relative to the vault, `Root` for the top level) | Moves a note into another folder. Wikilinks resolve by note name, so they keep working. |
| `rename_memory` | W | `path` (string, required), `new_name` (string, required) | Renames a note in its folder. |
| `upload_image` | W | `path` (string, required: the note the image belongs to), `name` (string, required, e.g. `diagram.png`), `data` (string, required: base64 or a `data:image/...;base64,` URL), `alt` (string), `append` (boolean, default false) | Stores a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF in the note's own folder (checked by content; the upload limit in Settings, Images applies, 5 MB by default). Identical bytes reuse the existing file; a taken name gets `-1`, `-2` ...: `{ok, path, name, bytes, url, markdown}`. Show it in the note with the returned `markdown` line, `![alt](path:name.png)`; `append: true` adds that line to the end of the note. The image then moves, goes to the Trash, is restored and is deleted with its note. |
| `list_images` | R | `folder` (string; `Root` or empty for the top level) or `path` (a note) | The images of one folder (not its sub folders), each with `used_in` (the notes and sections that show it); with `path`, the images that note shows and every image of its folder. |

### Search (`search`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_stats` | R | none | Counts of notes, links and folders. |
| `search_memory` | R | `q` (string, required; `query` is accepted as an alias), `limit` (integer, default 12) | Search titles and bodies. Supports `tag:x` and `#x`. |

### Query (`query`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_memory` | R | `folder`, `tags`, `author`, `type`, `status` (strings), `limit` (integer, default 50) | Filter notes by frontmatter. |
| `find_similar` | R | `path` (string, required), `limit` (integer, default 8) | Notes most similar to one note (shared tags and words). |
| `suggest_links` | R | `path` (string, required), `limit` (integer, default 8) | Similar notes not yet linked from this one. |
| `list_tags` | R | none | Every tag with its usage count. |
| `rename_tag` | W | `old` (string, required), `new` (string, required) | Renames a tag across the vault. |
| `merge_tag` | W | `a` (string, required), `b` (string, required) | Merges tag `a` into tag `b` across every note. |

### Tags (`tag`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_tags` | R | `path` (string; not in the advertised schema) | Every tag with its count, or the tags of one note when `path` is given. |
| `search_by_tag` | R | `tag` (string, required), `limit` (integer, default 50; not in the advertised schema) | Every note carrying a tag. |
| `add_tags` | W | `path` (string, required), `tags` (string, required, comma-separated) | Adds tags to a note. A leading `#` is stripped. |
| `remove_tags` | W | `path` (string, required), `tags` (string, required, comma-separated) | Removes tags from a note. |
| `set_tags` | W | `path` (string, required), `tags` (string, required, comma-separated) | Replaces a note's tag list. |

### Folders (`folder`, `ops`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_folders` | R | none | `{count, folders: [{name, count, color}]}`. |
| `create_folder` | W | `name` (string, required) | Creates a folder. |
| `rename_folder` | W | `folder` (string, required), `name` (string, required, one segment) | Renames a folder in place. Notes, sub folders, color and icon move along. |
| `move_folder` | W | `folder` (string, required), `into` (string; empty or `Root` = top level) | Moves a folder with everything in it. |
| `move_folder_contents` | W | `folder` (string, required), `into` (string; empty = top level) | Moves everything inside a folder into another folder, then removes the empty folder. Name clashes get a `-N` suffix. |
| `delete_folder` | W | `folder` (string, required), `into` (string), `mode` (`move` or `trash`) | Deletes a folder. By default its notes (at any depth) move to the folder's parent (Root for a top-level folder), keeping the sub folder structure below it; wikilinks to them are rewritten. `into` sends them to another existing folder instead (`Root` = top level). `mode: "trash"` moves every note to `.Trash` instead (`list_trash` / `restore_trash` bring them back) and cannot be combined with `into`. Other files in the folder are deleted. |
| `folder_stats` | R | `folder` (string, required) | Note count and metadata for one folder. |
| `get_folder_meta` | R | `folder` (string) | Color, icon and description of one folder, or of every folder. |
| `set_folder_meta` | W | `folder` (string, required), `color`, `icon`, `desc` (strings) | Sets folder display metadata. A field sent as an empty string is cleared. |

### Graph (`graph`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_graph` | R | none | Whole graph: `{nodes: [{id, path, folder, color, degree, tags, mtime}], links: [{source, target}]}`. |
| `get_neighbors` | R | `path` (string, required), `depth` (integer, default 1) | Notes within N hops. |
| `get_subgraph` | R | `path` (string, required), `depth` (integer, default 1), `max_nodes` (integer, default 60) | Subgraph around one note. |
| `find_path` | R | `source` (string, required), `target` (string, required) | Shortest wikilink path between two notes. |
| `get_hubs` | R | `limit` (integer, default 10) | Most connected notes. |
| `get_isolated` | R | none | Notes with no links in or out. |
| `link_stats` | R | `path` (string, required) | Outgoing, incoming and unresolved links of one note. |
| `broken_links` | R | none | Wikilinks pointing at notes that do not exist. |

### Versioning (`version`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_history` | R | `path` (string, required), `limit` (integer, default 20, at least 1) | Git history of a note, newest first, always an array of `{rev, date, author, message, version, total}` (plus `path` for commits under an earlier name: the history follows renames). `author` is the agent or user whose call made the change. `version` numbers the revisions from 1 (the oldest) to `total` (the current one), whatever `limit` is. |
| `get_note_at` | R | `path` (string, required), `rev` (string, required) | `{ok, path, rev, content}` at a revision. `rev` is one revision: a `rev` from `get_history`, `snap-<label>`, `HEAD~1` or `HEAD@{<date>}`. Unknown revisions, dates before the history and empty `rev` are errors. |
| `diff` | R | `path` (string, required), `rev_a` (string, required), `rev_b` (string) | `{path, from, to, changed, diff}` between two revisions, or `rev_a` against the current note. Ranges (`a..b`) and unknown revisions are errors. |
| `restore_memory` | W | `path` (string, required), `rev` (string, required) | Restores a note to a revision (a new commit). Give the current path; content under an earlier name is found. Restoring the old path of a renamed note is refused and names the current one. |
| `snapshot` | W | `label` (string, required) | Commits pending changes and tags the last commit `snap-<label>` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; spaces become `-`; at most 40 characters; must be new). Use the tag as `rev`. |
| `soft_delete` | W | `path` (string, required) | Moves a note to `.Trash` and remembers where it came from. |
| `list_trash` | R | none | Notes in `.Trash`, newest first: `{name, path, original, deleted, by, title}` (`by` = `{id, name, kind}` of who deleted it, null when unknown). |
| `restore_trash` | W | `name` (string, required; `.md` optional), `into` (string) | Restores a note from `.Trash` to the path it was deleted from, or into the folder `into` (`Root` = top level). |

All versioning tools except `soft_delete`, `list_trash` and `restore_trash`
need version history on (see [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md#version-history));
otherwise they answer "version history is off".

### Bulk writes (`write`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_create` | W | `notes` (array, required) of `{title (required), folder (default `Memory`), content}` | Creates many notes in one call; titles and folders follow `create_memory`. Every item is checked first and nothing is created when one is malformed (missing title, wrong type, unknown key). The reply has one result per item: `{ok, path}` or `{ok: false, item, title, error}`. |
| `duplicate_memory` | W | `path` (string, required) | Copies a note as `<name>-copy` in the same folder (a long name is shortened so the suffix fits in 80 characters). |
| `merge_memory` | W | `paths` (array of strings, required: existing notes, each once, not `into`), `into` (string, required; `.md` optional) | Appends the body of each source, without its frontmatter, to `into` under `## from <name>`, and adds the sources' tags to the target's tags. `into` is created when missing. The sources are kept. Returns `{ok, into, created, merged, sources, tags_added}`. |
| `template_create` | W | `template` (string, required; a note in `Templates/`, as `Meeting` or `Meeting.md`), `title` (string, required), `folder` (string, default `Root`), `variables` (object) | Creates a note from a template with `{{var}}` substitution. `{{title}}` (the note title) and `{{date}}` (today, `YYYY-MM-DD`) are built in unless given in `variables`. Only notes in `Templates/` can be templates. |
| `bulk_replace` | W | `find` (string, required), `replace` (string, required), `folder` (string), `regex` (boolean, default false), `dry_run` (boolean, default false) | Find and replace across notes. `find` must not be empty or (with `regex`) match an empty string. `folder` includes its subfolders (`Root` = top level only); a missing folder is an error. With `regex`, `replace` expands `$1` / `${name}` (`$$` is a literal `$`); unknown groups are errors. Needs `write` even with `dry_run`. |
| `bulk_delete` | W | `paths` (array of strings), `folder` (string) | Moves many notes to `.Trash` (recoverable with `restore_trash`), by list and / or folder (with subfolders). Any invalid path (missing, outside the vault, a folder, not a note) refuses the whole call and is listed. |

### Collaboration (`collab`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lock_node` | W | `path` (string, required), `owner` (string, default the caller), `ttl` (integer seconds, default 300) | Soft lock on a note. |
| `release_lock` | W | `path` (string, required), `owner` (string, default the caller) | Releases a lock. |
| `get_locks` | R | none | Active locks. |
| `mention_agent` | W | `agent` (string, required), `path` (string, required), `message` (string) | Writes `> @agent: message` into a note. With agent `mnemo`, Memora's own agent answers it in the note (the request is struck through and the reply quoted under it). |
| `get_assignments` | R | `agent` (string) | Notes with `assigned_to` in their frontmatter. |

### Activity and health (`ops`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_events` | R | `since` (number, unix time), `folder`, `actor` (strings), `limit` (integer, default 50) | Recent note created, updated and deleted events. |
| `presence` | R | `window` (integer seconds, default 300) | Agents active within the window. |
| `get_logs` | R | `range` (string, default `1d`; also `7d`, `today`, `yesterday`), `actor` (string), `limit` (integer, default 100) | Activity log for a period. |
| `search_logs` | R | `q` (string, required), `range` (string, default `7d`), `actor` (string), `limit` (integer, default 100) | Keyword search in the activity log. |
| `digest` | R | `folder` (string), `since` (number) | Event counts per actor and per type. |
| `healthcheck` | R | none | Note count, broken links, orphans and git status. |
| `stale_detection` | R | `days` (integer, default 30) | Notes untouched for more than N days. |

### Identity (`identity`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set_my_name` | W | `name` (string, required) | Sets the display alias shown in the activity feed and log. |
| `set_my_color` | W | `color` (string, required; `#rrggbb`, or `""` to reset) | Sets the calling API key's display color. Fails for browser sessions. |
| `list_actors` | R | none | `{me, aliases}`: the caller and every known alias. |

### Import and export (`interop`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `export_memory` | W | `paths` (array of strings, required; notes or folders), `out_path` (string), `overwrite` (boolean, default false) | Writes a zip of the given paths to the server's exchange folder and returns `{ok, path, name, bytes, replaced}`, where `path` and `name` are the zip's file name. Every path must exist; missing ones are listed and nothing is written. `out_path` is a plain file name ending in `.zip` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, at most 120 characters); the default is `memora-export-<unix seconds>.zip`. An existing zip of that name is only replaced with `overwrite: true`. |
| `import_memory` | W | `zip_path` (string, required), `overwrite` (boolean, default false) | Imports the `.md` notes of a zip in the exchange folder, by the file name `export_memory` returned. Returns `{ok, added, overwritten, skipped, unsafe, failed}`: `skipped` are existing notes kept (no `overwrite`), `unsafe` are entries with an absolute or escaping path (`{entry, reason}`), `failed` are entries too large or unreadable. |

The exchange folder is `exchange` in the state directory (`<MEMORA_STATE>/exchange`),
one per Memora instance, created with mode 0700.
Tools never read or write anywhere else on the server's disk.

### Checks, to-dos and pins (`ux`)

| Tool | | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_todos` | R | `path` (string) | Open checklist items (`- [ ]`) in one note or the whole vault. |
| `follow_ups` | R | none | Notes whose status is still awaiting action. |
| `validate_memory` | R | `path` (string, required) | Checks a note: frontmatter present and well formed, a valid `created` date, tags, and broken links (named in the issue and listed in `broken_links`). |
| `list_pins` | R | none | The owner's pinned notes and folders in sidebar order: `{count, pins:[{kind, path, position, missing}]}`. `missing` is true when the path no longer exists (renamed or deleted outside Memora). |
| `pin` | W | `path` (string, required), `kind` (`note` or `folder`; default: what the path is on disk), `position` (integer from 0; default: the end) | Pins an existing note or folder, or moves its pin. A note path may leave out `.md`. At most 200 pins. Returns the list. |
| `unpin` | W | `path` (string, required), `kind` | Removes a pin; the note or folder is not touched. Returns the list with `removed`. |

Pins are shared by every browser of the owner (`/api/pins`). They follow their note or
folder through renames and moves done by Memora (over MCP or HTTP, including notes inside
a moved folder) and are removed when the item is deleted or moved to the trash; deleting a
folder removes every pin under it. A key whose privacy rules hide a path neither lists
nor changes its pin, and `position` counts only the pins the key can see.

### Admin tools (`admin`)

Listed and callable only for keys with the `admin` scope (and for browser
sessions). They are not part of the switchable catalog: global tool switches and
a key's tool list do not apply to them, and they do not need `write`.

| Tool | Arguments | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `admin_list_tools` | none | `{tools: [{name, category, description, enabled}]}` for every catalog tool. |
| `admin_set_tool` | `name` (string, required), `enabled` (boolean, required) | Switches a catalog tool on or off for every key. Returns `{ok, name, enabled}`. |
| `privacy_list` | `path` (string), `kind` (`node` or `folder`) | Without `path`: every privacy rule. With `path`: that note or folder's own rule, the folder rules it inherits, and which agents can see it. |
| `privacy_set` | `path` (string, required), `agents` (array of key ids or names, required; a comma-separated string also works), `kind` (`node` or `folder`), `mode` (`deny` or `allow_only`, default `deny`) | Replaces the rule on a path. `deny` hides it from the listed agents; `allow_only` hides it from every other agent, including keys created later. `deny` with no agents removes the rule. A node rule follows its note through renames and moves. |
| `privacy_clear` | `path` (string, required), `kind` (`node` or `folder`) | Removes the path's own rule. Rules on parent folders still apply. |

When `kind` is omitted it is taken from the path on disk: a folder if a folder
exists there, otherwise a note.

## Identity and tracking

Every tool call is published to the web UI's realtime activity stream as an
`ai_activity` start and end pair, named after the API key (or the signed-in
user), with the note paths involved. Calls are also counted per key: the Keys
page and `GET /api/keys` show each key's `uses`, `last_ip`, and the tools it has
called recently. `initialize` registers the connection under the key's name
(`GET /api/aliases`). `set_my_name` changes the alias shown in the activity
feed and log, and `set_my_color` changes the key's color in the UI. See
[API.md](API.md) for the HTTP endpoints.

title: HTTP API
text:
# HTTP API

The `memora` binary serves the HTTP API, the MCP endpoint, the OAuth endpoints,
the web UI, and the WebSocket on one port. This document lists the HTTP endpoints.

## Authentication

The Auth column in the tables below uses these levels:

- None: reachable without credentials.
- Session: requires the `memora_sess` cookie set by a successful login.
- Key (`scope`): an API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`
  that carries the named scope.
- Session or key (`scope`): either of the above.
- Session only: an API key is not enough. API keys get `401` (or `403` where noted).
- +CSRF: the same-origin check described below applies.

### API key scopes

A key carries any of the scopes `mcp`, `read`, `write`, and `admin`. New keys get
`mcp`, `read`, and `write` unless other scopes are requested. The scope a route
needs is decided by its path and method:

| Scope | Routes |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | `/mcp` |
| `admin` | `/api/tools`, `/api/keys` and `/api/keys/*`, `/api/access` and `/api/access/*`, `/api/logs/settings`, `/api/settings/server`, `/api/oauth/clients` and `/api/oauth/clients/*`, `/api/privacy` and `/api/privacy/*`, `/api/trash/delete`, `/api/trash/empty`; deleting for good with `/api/delete` |
| `read` | Every other `GET` or `HEAD` under `/api/` |
| `write` | Every other method under `/api/` |

A key without the needed scope gets `403 {error, required_scope}`. A missing key
gets `401`; for `/mcp` the `401` carries a `WWW-Authenticate` header,
`Bearer resource_metadata="<base>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`, so OAuth
capable clients can start sign-in. An invalid key gets `401` and is logged; an
IP that keeps presenting invalid keys is put on a cooldown (`429`).

`/api/auth/*` never accepts an API key: without a valid session it answers `401`.

API keys see the vault through their privacy rules (see [Privacy](#privacy)):
notes and folders hidden from a key behave as if they do not exist. A browser
session sees everything.

### CSRF

Write endpoints that accept a session check the request origin whenever a
session cookie is present: `Origin` (or, without it, `Referer`) must match the
request `Host` (or an `X-Forwarded-Host` sent by a trusted proxy), and
`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is refused. A failed check is
`403 {"error":"origin mismatch"}`. Requests without a session cookie (API-key
clients) pass, since a browser cannot attach an API key on its own.

The public auth forms (`/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/verify`,
`/api/auth/bootstrap`, `/api/auth/reset`) also refuse a foreign or `null`
`Origin` when no cookie exists yet. A request with neither `Origin` nor
`Referer` (curl, the CLI) passes.

### Locked instance

While the instance is LOCKED, `/api/*` and `/mcp` answer
`423 {error, locked: true, hint}` except for `/api/auth/state`, `/api/auth/verify`,
`/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/logout`, `/api/auth/bootstrap`, and
`/api/auth/reset`. Other pages redirect to `/login?locked=1`; static assets,
`/login`, `/logout`, `/healthz`, and `/favicon.ico` are still served.
`/api/auth/login` itself answers `423` while locked.

### Vault not configured

Until a vault folder is configured, `/mcp` and every `/api/*` route except
`/api/auth/*`, `/api/settings*`, `/api/config`, `/api/keys*`, `/api/tools`,
`/api/access*`, and `/api/ui/*` answer
`409 {"error":"vault not configured", "needs_vault":true}`.

### Limits and other gates

- Requests for a host outside the configured domain list get a bare `404`.
- Access rules (see `/api/access`) can block a caller:
  `403 {"error":"access denied by stack rule", ip}`.
- Per-IP rate limits answer `429` with a `Retry-After` header and
  `{error, limited, cooldown, retry_after}`. Login, code check, setup, reset, profile,
  password, and username changes have a stricter limit and a cooldown after
  repeated failed attempts. Requests from the machine itself and `/healthz` are
  not limited.
- A request that takes longer than 30 seconds is answered with `408`.
- A password hashing pool that is busy answers `503` with `Retry-After: 2`.
- `GET` answers under `/api/` (except `/api/auth/*`) are gzip-compressed when the
  request sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. Pages, writes, sign-in, `/mcp` and
  server-sent events are never compressed.

Responses are JSON unless stated otherwise. Errors are `{"error": "..."}`. Vault
errors map to `404` for not-found (including paths hidden from the caller) and
`400` for bad input.

## Health and discovery

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/healthz` | None | `{ok, server}` for unauthenticated callers from other machines. A signed-in browser or a caller on the same machine gets `{ok, server, version, vault_configured, vault, armed, locked, base_url, base_url_configured}`. |
| GET | `/.well-known/mcp.json` | None | The MCP discovery card: `{name, version, description, mcp, auth, capabilities, tools, resources}`. `tools` lists the full catalog with `enabled` per tool. |
| GET | `/tools` | None | An HTML rendering of the tool catalog. A signed-in browser gets the app shell instead. |
| POST | `/mcp` | Key (`mcp`), or Session (+CSRF) | MCP over streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC in, JSON-RPC out). See [MCP.md](MCP.md). A session has full access; a key is limited by its tool grant. Notifications get `202` with no body. Malformed JSON is `400` with a JSON-RPC error. Other methods get `405` with `Allow: POST`. |

## Auth

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/auth/state` | None | `{bootstrap, realm, min_password_len, gateway, armed, locked, setup_hint, ready, checks:{vault, state}, code_required, cooldown, vault_configured}`. Adds `signed_out` (`password_changed` or `signed_out_remotely`) when the browser's session was ended on purpose, and `mode`, `expires_in`, `ttl` while a setup or reset window is open. |
| POST | `/api/auth/verify` | None (+CSRF) | Checks the setup code shown on the server before the setup or reset form is shown. Body: `{code}`. Returns `{ok, mode, expires_in, user}`. `403` when no window is open or the instance is not ready. A wrong code answers `403 {error, burned:false}` and counts against the caller IP's budget of 3 wrong codes (then `429`); after 50 wrong codes in one window the window closes and the code is void: `403 {error, burned:true}`. |
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | None (+CSRF) | `{ok, user, expires_in, redirect}` and sets the session cookie. Body: `{username, password}`. `400` when a field is missing, `401` on bad credentials, `403` if the account is disabled, `423` if locked, `429` during a cooldown of the caller IP (there is no account-wide lockout; see DEPLOYMENT.md, Failed sign-ins). |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | None (+CSRF) | `{ok:true}`. Ends the session named by the cookie, if any, and clears the cookie. |
| POST | `/api/auth/bootstrap` | None (+CSRF) | Creates the owner account. Body: `{code, username, password}`. Returns `{ok, user, redirect, persisted}` and sets a session cookie. The username is stored lowercase. `400` for an invalid username or password length; `403` unless a window is open, the code is right, the instance is ready, and no account exists. |
| POST | `/api/auth/reset` | None (+CSRF) | Sets a new password for the single account, and may rename it. Body: `{code, username, password}`. Returns `{ok, user, persisted}`. Signs out every session. `400` for invalid input; `403` unless a window is open, the code is right, and an account exists. |
| POST | `/api/auth/profile` | Session only (+CSRF) | With `password` in the body, changes the password exactly like `POST /api/settings/password` (body `{current, password, confirm}`). Otherwise sets `display_name` (at most 48 characters) and returns `{ok, changed, persisted, user, password_changed:false}`; with no `display_name` it returns `{ok, changed:false}`. |
| GET | `/api/auth/me` | Session only | `{authenticated, user, enabled, expires_in}`. `401` without a session. |
| GET | `/api/auth/events` | Session only | Recent entries of the security activity log, newest first: `{events:[{at, event, ip, user, detail, actor, actor_kind, actor_id}], count}`. `user` is the stored actor (`key:<id>` for API-key calls); `actor` is the display name (the key's current name, falling back to its id; the username for the browser), `actor_kind` is `agent` or `user` (null when there is no actor). Query: `limit` (default 200, max 2000), `q`. |

## Pages

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/login` | None | The sign-in page. A signed-in browser is redirected to `/` unless the instance is locked or the query has `oauth` (the OAuth consent card). |
| POST | `/logout` | None (+CSRF) | Ends the session, clears the cookie, and redirects to `/login`. With a session cookie the request must be same-origin (`403` otherwise); other methods get `405`. The web UI uses `POST /api/auth/logout`. |
| GET | `/`, `/index.html` | Session | The web app shell. Without a session: `302` to `/login`. `503` when the UI assets are not installed. |
| GET | App routes (see below) | Session | The same app shell as `/`. Without a session: `302` to `/login?r=<path>`, so sign-in returns to the page. |

App routes are the web app's client-side pages: `/brain`, `/nodes`, `/graph`,
`/canvas`, `/tags`, `/activity`, `/agents`, `/access`, `/settings`,
`/overview`, `/welcome`, `/trash`, `/mnemo`, the older names `/home`, `/vault`, `/logs`, `/keys`,
and `/node/` or `/node/<percent-encoded vault path>`. The path is never used to
read a file; a path holding NUL or another control character (raw or
percent-encoded) is `400`. `/tools` is an app route for a signed-in browser and
the public tool catalog otherwise.

HTML pages are sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`
and a per-response CSP nonce.

Any other `GET` that asks for HTML (`Accept: text/html`), is outside `/api/`,
`/mcp`, `/oauth`, and `/.well-known`, and has no file extension in its last
segment gets the app shell (which shows its "page not found" view). Every other
unmatched request is `404 {"error":"not found"}`.

## Static assets

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets/{name}` | None | Static UI assets (whitelisted filenames only, else `404`). |
| GET | `/app.js`, `/app.css`, `/login.css` | None | The UI bundle and styles. Revalidated on every load (`Cache-Control: no-cache`, ETag). |
| GET | `/favicon.svg` | None | The icon. |
| GET | `/favicon.ico` | None | `204` with no body. |
| GET | `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/sw.js`, `/robots.txt`, `/offline.html`, `/icon-192.png`, `/icon-512.png`, `/icon-maskable-512.png`, `/apple-touch-icon.png` | None | PWA files and `robots.txt`. Images and the manifest are cached for 5 minutes; code is revalidated on every load. |

## Vault

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/tree` | Session or key (`read`) | Notes grouped by folder: `{folder: [{path, name, folder, mtime, title}]}`; `title` is what the app shows (front matter `title`, else the first `# heading`, else the file name with `_` as spaces). |
| GET | `/api/folders` | Session or key (`read`) | Every folder the caller may see, empty and nested ones included (`{folders:[path]}`); dot folders such as `.Trash` are left out. |
| GET | `/api/note` | Session or key (`read`) | `{path, name, content, html, tags, frontmatter, backlinks, size, mtime}`. Query: `path` (`400` when empty). |
| GET | `/api/vault/file` | Session or key (`read`) | The raw bytes of one image file in the vault (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO; never SVG). Query: `path` (vault-relative). The file content must match its type. At most 10 MiB (`413`). Sent with an `ETag` (`304` on `If-None-Match`), `Cache-Control: private, max-age=300`, and a sandbox CSP. `400` invalid path, `403` path not allowed, `404` not found, `415` not an image. |
| GET | `/api/folder-meta` | Session or key (`read`) | Folder metadata keyed by folder name. Query: `folder` (optional). |
| POST | `/api/save` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, path}`. Body: `{path, content}`. Overwrites the note. |
| POST | `/api/create` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, path}`. Body: `{title, folder?, content?}`. |
| POST | `/api/rename` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, path}` with the new path. Body: `{path, name}`. |
| POST | `/api/move` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, path}` with the new path. Body: `{path, folder?}`. |
| POST | `/api/delete` | Session or key (`write`; `admin` to delete for good, +CSRF) | `{ok:true}`. Body: `{path, mode?}`. Deletes the note for good (no trash); with version history on, its earlier versions are erased from the history too, so nothing can bring it back. Because that cannot be undone, an API key needs the `admin` scope for it (`403 {error, required_scope: "admin"}` otherwise, as MCP `delete_memory` with `permanent`); the owner's browser session may. `mode: "trash"` (what the web app sends) moves it to `.Trash` instead, remembering where it was and who deleted it: `{ok, trashed, to}`. |
| GET | `/api/trash` | Session or key (`read`) | Notes in `.Trash` the caller may see, newest first: `{items: [{name, path, original, deleted, by, title}]}` (`by` = `{id, name, kind}`, null when unknown). Nothing is removed automatically. |
| POST | `/api/trash/restore` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | Body: `{name, into?}`. Back to where the note was deleted from (or into the folder `into`); a taken name gets `-1`, `-2` ...: `{ok, path, from, renamed?}`. 404 when the name is not in the trash. |
| POST | `/api/trash/delete` | Session or key (`admin`, +CSRF) | Body: `{name}`. Deletes one trash entry for good: `{ok, deleted, name, history?}`. With version history on, the note is also erased from the history (every earlier version under every name it had, its trash record and its path in commit messages), and `history` is `{erased, ms, commits}`. Other notes keep their versions; their revision ids change. |
| POST | `/api/trash/empty` | Session or key (`admin`, +CSRF) | Deletes every trash entry the caller may see, for good: `{ok, count, names, history?}`, erasing them from the version history in one rewrite (as `/api/trash/delete`). |
| POST | `/api/folder` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, path}`. Body: `{name}`. |
| POST | `/api/folder/rename` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, from, to, notes}`. Body: `{folder, name}`. |
| POST | `/api/folder/move` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | Moves a folder and everything in it. `{ok, from, to, notes}`. Body: `{folder, into}`; `into` empty or `Root` means the top level. |
| POST | `/api/folder/move-contents` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | Moves everything inside a folder into another one, then removes the emptied folder. Name clashes get a `-N` suffix. `{ok, from, to, moved}`. Body: `{folder, into}`; `into` empty or `Root` means the top level. |
| POST | `/api/delete-folder` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | Deletes a folder. Body: `{folder, into?, mode?}`. By default its notes move to the folder's parent (the top level for a top-level folder), keeping the sub folder structure below it, and wikilinks are rewritten: `{ok, deleted_folder, moved_to, moved, links_updated}` (`moved` lists the new paths; `moved_to_root` repeats it when they went to the top level). `into` names another existing folder for the notes (`Root` = top level). `mode: "trash"` moves every note to `.Trash` instead (restorable from the Trash on the Notes page, `/api/trash/restore`, or the MCP tools `list_trash` / `restore_trash`): `{ok, deleted_folder, mode, count, trashed}`. Other files in the folder are deleted. |
| POST | `/api/folder-meta` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | `{ok, folder}`. Body: `{folder, color?, icon?, desc?}`. |

The three folder operations also publish a `folder_changed` realtime event so
open browsers reload their tree.

### Version history

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/history?path=&limit=` | Session or key (`read`) | A note's revisions, newest first (the vault's git history, following renames): `{path, total, versions: [{rev, date, author, message, version, total, path?, owner}]}`. `version` counts from 1 (the oldest) to `total` (the current one); `owner` is true when the signed-in owner made the change. `limit` defaults to 100 (at most 500). |
| GET | `/api/note-at?path=&rev=` | Session or key (`read`) | The note as it was at one revision (a `rev` from `/api/history`, `snap-<label>`, `HEAD~1`, `HEAD@{<date>}`): `{path, rev, content, html}`, `html` rendered like `/api/note`. |

### Images

Images live in the folder of the note that shows them, and a note shows one with
`![alt](path:name.png)` (`path:` names a file in the note's own folder). Saving a
note that points with `path:Other/Folder/pic.png` to an image elsewhere copies that
image beside the note and rewrites the link, so notes never point across folders.
Images follow their note: a move carries them, the Trash keeps them in
`.Trash/.assets/<entry>/` until the note is restored (to the same or another
folder) or deleted for good, and a deleted folder takes its images along. An image
that another note of the same folder still shows is copied or kept instead.

| POST | `/api/vault/image?note=<path>&name=<file>` | Session or key (`write`, +CSRF) | The raw image bytes as the body (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, checked by content). Stored beside the note; identical bytes reuse the existing file, a taken name gets `-1`, `-2` ...: `{ok, path, name, bytes, url, markdown}` (`markdown` is the line to put in the note). `400` for another file type, a size above the upload limit, or a missing note. |

Privacy rules hide notes or folders from chosen agents (API keys). A rule has a

## OAuth

Memora is an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for remote MCP clients. Only the
authorization code flow with PKCE (`S256`) is supported. The access token is a
new API key named after the client, with the default scopes (`mcp`, `read`,
`write`) and every tool; it appears on the Agents page like any other key and
is revoked by deleting or disabling that key. URLs in the metadata use
`MEMORA_BASE_URL` when it is set, else the scheme and host of the request.

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` | None | Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728): `{resource, authorization_servers, bearer_methods_supported, scopes_supported, resource_name}`. |
| GET | `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp`, `/.well-known/openid-configuration` | None | Authorization server metadata (RFC 8414): `issuer`, the authorization, token, and registration endpoints, supported response types (`code`), grant types (`authorization_code`, `refresh_token`), PKCE methods (`S256`), token endpoint auth methods, `scopes_supported` (`mcp`), and `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`. |
| POST | `/oauth/register` | None | Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591). Body: `{redirect_uris, client_name?}`. `redirect_uris` holds 1 to 10 URIs, each HTTPS or plain HTTP on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`, without a fragment. Returns `201 {client_id, client_name, redirect_uris, client_id_issued_at, token_endpoint_auth_method, grant_types, response_types}`. `400 {error, error_description}` for invalid metadata or when 500 clients are registered. `429` past 10 registrations from one IP (then one per minute). A client that has not completed an authorization within an hour is removed; it can register again. |
| GET | `/oauth/authorize` | None | `302` to `/login?oauth=1&<query>`, where the sign-in page shows a consent card (after sign-in when needed). |
| POST | `/oauth/token` | None | Form-encoded or JSON body. `grant_type=authorization_code` with `code`, `code_verifier`, `client_id` (or HTTP Basic), and optional `redirect_uri`; or `grant_type=refresh_token` with `refresh_token` and optional `client_id`. Returns `{access_token, token_type:"Bearer", refresh_token, scope:"mcp"}`. Codes are single use and expire after 10 minutes. A refresh gives the same key a new secret and a new refresh token. Errors are `400 {error, error_description}` (`invalid_request`, `invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type`). |
| GET | `/api/oauth/request` | None | What the consent card shows for an authorization request. Query: the `/oauth/authorize` query. Returns `{ok:true, client:{id, name, kind}, redirect_host, signed_in, user}` or `{ok:false, error, error_description, redirect}`. |
| POST | `/api/oauth/approve` | Session only (+CSRF) | Body: `{query, allow}` where `query` is the authorization request query. Returns `{ok:true, redirect}`: the client's redirect URI with a `code` when `allow` is `true`, else with `error=access_denied`. An invalid request returns `{ok:false, error, error_description, redirect}`. `401` without a session. |
| GET | `/api/oauth/clients` | Session or key (`admin`) | `{clients:[{client_id, name, redirect_uris, kind, created_at, fetched_at}], connections:[{key_id, client_id}]}`. `kind` is `dcr` (registered), `cimd` (metadata document), or `manual` (added by the owner). |
| POST | `/api/oauth/clients` | Session or key (`admin`, +CSRF) | Registers a client by hand. Body: `{name?, redirect_uris}`. Returns `{ok, client}`. `400` for invalid redirect URIs. |
| POST | `/api/oauth/clients/delete` | Session or key (`admin`, +CSRF) | Forgets a client and its refresh tokens. Body: `{client_id}`. Returns `{ok, deleted}`. Keys issued to the client stay until they are deleted. |

A `client_id` may also be an HTTPS URL of a client metadata document. The
server fetches it (public addresses only, no redirects, at most 64 KiB), checks
that its `client_id` matches the URL, and caches it for 24 hours.

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/ws` | Session only | WebSocket upgrade. The `Origin` must be same-origin (`403` otherwise). `503` when too many clients are connected. |
| POST | `/_bus` | Loopback only | Publishes a JSON object (at most 64 KiB) into the event stream. Returns `{ok:true}`. `403` for callers that are not on the same machine, that come through a proxy (any forwarding header) or that are a web page (an `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-*` header), `400` for a body that is not a JSON object, `413` for a body or event that is too large. |

### Local stop

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/_stop` | Loopback and stop token | Stops the server gracefully, like Ctrl+C (open requests finish, buffered usage is written). Returns `{ok:true}` and exits shortly after. `403` unless the caller is on the same machine, not behind a proxy (any forwarding header), and sends the `X-Memora-Stop-Token` header. At startup, once the port is bound, the server writes a fresh random token to
`<state>/stop.token` (readable by the server's user only on Linux and macOS)
and removes it on exit. `memora-cli stop` reads that file and calls `/_stop`
first on every OS; only if that fails does it fall back to SIGTERM (Linux,
macOS) or `taskkill` (Windows, where a server started without a console
ignores a polite `taskkill`). Anyone who can read the state folder can stop
the server; they can already read its database.

### `ai_activity` events

Every MCP `tools/call` publishes a `start` and an `end` event sharing `call_id`:

```json
{"type":"ai_activity","phase":"start","call_id":"c1a2b3c4d5e6-0","actor":"research-bot",
 "actor_kind":"agent","actor_id":"k_1a2b3c4d","action":"read_memory","label":"Plan/Index.md",
 "paths":["Plan/Index.md"],"_ts":1760600000.12}
{"type":"ai_activity","phase":"end","call_id":"c1a2b3c4d5e6-0","actor":"research-bot",
 "actor_kind":"agent","actor_id":"k_1a2b3c4d","action":"read_memory","label":"Plan/Index.md",
 "paths":["Plan/Index.md"],"ok":true,"ms":2,"_ts":1760600000.12}
```

- `actor`: the API key's name (fallback: key id) with `actor_kind: "agent"`; for a
  browser session the username with `actor_kind: "user"`. `actor_id` is the key id (or
  the username). Node events (`node_created`, ...) from the call carry the same `actor`.
- `action`: the tool name.
- `for` (optional): who the agent acted for and how it was asked. Mnemo, the built-in
  agent (`actor: "Mnemo"`, `actor_id: "mnemo"`), sets it: `owner · chat`,
  `owner · console`, `<who> · @mnemo in <note>`.
- `paths`: vault-relative note paths from the arguments (`path`, `paths`, `from`, `to`,
  `old_path`, `new_path`, `into` of `merge_memory`, `source`/`target` of `find_path`)
  plus note paths found in the result (search hits, the created or moved note), at
  most 20, each at most 512 bytes (longer paths are dropped). Whole-vault overviews
  (`get_graph`, `list_memory`, logs, ...) add no result paths.
- Read-only tools publish `start` after running (so it carries the result paths),
  immediately followed by `end`; mutating tools publish `start` before running and `end`
  after, with the result paths added.
- `end` adds `ok`, `ms`, and on failure `error` (at most 200 characters). `label` is at
  most 160 characters. `_ts` is the publish time in unix seconds. `end` events are
  realtime only: they are not written to `.events.jsonl` or the replay buffer.
