## Pins

The owner's pinned notes and folders (the sidebar's Pinned list), shared by every
browser and device of the instance.

| Method | Path | Auth | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/pins` | Session only | `{count, pins:[{kind, path, position, missing}]}` in display order. |
| PUT | `/api/pins` | Session only (+CSRF) | Same as GET. Body: `{pins:[{kind, path}]}`, the whole ordered list (reorder, remove). |
| POST | `/api/pins/pin` | Session only (+CSRF) | Same as GET. Body: `{kind, path, position?}`. Pins an existing note or folder at `position` (default: the end), or moves its pin there; `404` if it does not exist. |
| POST | `/api/pins/unpin` | Session only (+CSRF) | Same as GET plus `removed`. Body: `{kind, path}`. |

`kind` is `note` or `folder`. `path` is vault-relative as the tree shows it (notes end in
`.md`): absolute paths, `..`, empty or hidden segments, `\`, control characters and paths
over 1024 characters get `400`, as do more than 200 pins. API keys get `403` (agents use
the MCP tools `list_pins`, `pin` and `unpin`). Bodies are limited to 256 KiB for `PUT`
and 8 KiB for `pin`/`unpin` (`413`). `missing` is true when the path no longer exists,
for example after a rename outside Memora; such a pin is kept until it is removed.

Renames, moves and deletes done by Memora (HTTP or MCP) rewrite or drop pins in the same
database transaction, including pins on notes and folders inside a moved folder;
moving an item to the trash or deleting it removes its pin, and deleting a folder
removes every pin under it. Every change publishes a `pins_changed` realtime event with
no other data; open browsers reload the list. Pins are stored in the `pin` table of
`memora.db`.

## Mnemo (built-in agent)

Mnemo is the notes agent built into Memora. Every route needs the signed-in
browser session (API keys get `403`, writes need CSRF); the console's `/mnemo`
uses a short local session. Mnemo's data lives in `assistant.sqlite3` beside
`memora.db` (file mode 0600): providers with their API keys sealed
(ChaCha20-Poly1305, the same key as the server's other secrets), models,
preferences, chats and messages. A key is never returned; providers carry a
four-character `key_hint`.

| Method | Path | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/assistant/state` | `{name, ready, providers, models, prefs, tools, defaults}`. `ready` is true when a model can answer. `tools` is the fixed list Mnemo may use. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/providers` | Adds or changes a provider. Body: `{id?, kind?, label?, api_style?, base_url?, api_key?, enabled?}`. Up to 20 providers, several of the same type allowed. `id` is the owner's own (1-32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`; made from `label` when left out; it cannot change, since models are keyed `id/model`). `kind` is `openai`, `anthropic` or `custom` (any OpenAI-compatible server, which needs `base_url`, its `/v1` address); `api_style` is `chat` or `responses` (OpenAI and compatible) or `messages` (Anthropic). For an existing `id`, fields left out keep their value, so `{id, enabled: false}` switches a provider off (its models leave the model pickers). Leaving `api_key` out keeps the saved key; `""` removes it. Returns the state plus `saved` (the id). |
| POST | `/api/assistant/providers/test` | Body: `{id}`. Lists the provider's models as a connection check: `{ok, models, ms}` or `{ok: false, error}`. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/providers/delete` | Body: `{id}`. Removes the provider, its key and its models. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/models/fetch` | Body: `{provider}`. Reads the provider's model list (`GET <base>/models`, every page for Anthropic) with the limits it reports: the context window from `max_input_tokens`, `context_length`, `context_window`, `max_context_length` or `max_model_len`, and the reply limit from `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens`. Pinned models stay; unpinned ones the provider no longer lists go. Returns the state plus `fetched`. `502` when the provider refuses. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/models` | Body: `{provider, model, label?, context_window?, max_output?, pinned?, hidden?}`. Adds a model by hand or changes it; `null` clears a limit. The app sets only pinned, hidden and new models; limits normally come from the provider. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/models/delete` | Body: `{provider, model}`. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/prefs` | Any of `default_model` (`provider/model`), `system_prompt` (up to 4000 characters), `temperature` (0-2), `max_output_tokens` (64-200000), `context_tokens` (2000-2000000, for models without a window), `max_steps` (1-30 tool rounds per reply), `launcher` (the floating button); `null` resets one. |
| GET | `/api/assistant/sessions` | `{sessions: [{id, title, scope, model, pinned, created_at, updated_at, messages}]}`. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions` | Body: `{scope?, model?, title?}`. `scope` is `global`, `note:<path>` or `folder:<path>`. Returns `{session}`. |
| GET | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}` | `{session, messages: [{id, role, content, tool_calls, tool_call_id, tool_name, meta, created_at}], context}`. `context` is `{used, window, reserved_output, compact_at, compactions, model}` for the model the chat would use now (approximate tokens), or `null` without a usable model. A message with `meta.compact: true` is a summary that stands in for every message before `meta.keep_from`. |
| GET | `/api/assistant/search` | Query `q` (every word must appear, any case), `limit` (default 60, at most 200). `{query, hits: [{chat, title, scope, message_id, role, snippet, at}]}`, newest first: the owner's messages and Mnemo's replies whose text or chat title holds the words; `message_id` is `null` for a chat matched by its title alone. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/rerun` | Body: `{message_id?, model?}` (default: the last of the owner's messages). Runs that message's turn again: every message after it is removed, then the reply streams as for `/chat`. `400` when `message_id` is not one of the owner's messages in the chat, `409` while it answers. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/steer` | Body: `{text}`. A message for the reply running in the chat: Mnemo reads it before its next step (stored as a user message with `meta.steer`, streamed as `steered {text}`). `409` when no reply is running. |
| GET | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/live` | The reply running in the chat as server-sent events: every event since it began, then live, until it ends. `204` when none is running. |
| GET | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/export` | The chat as a Markdown file (`text/markdown`, a download): each message with its time, Mnemo's steps, what it showed, compaction summaries. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/stop` | End the reply running in the chat. `{stopped}`. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/compact` | Fold the older turns into a summary now (the chat's model writes it; the last turn stays as it is). `{ok: true, messages, tokens, context}`, or `{ok: false, reason, context}` when there is nothing older yet. `409` while the chat is answering. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}` | Body: `{title?, model?, pinned?}`. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/delete` | Deletes the chat and its messages (notes are not touched). |
| POST | `/api/assistant/sessions/{id}/chat` | Body: `{text, model?, attach?, tz?, tz_offset?, answer?}` (`answer` `{to, approve?, other?}` answers one of Mnemo's questions by its call id; `approve` is set when the tapped option approves a change) (`tz` an IANA zone name and `tz_offset` minutes east of UTC, from the browser, for Mnemo's `current_time`). `attach` lists up to 8 items `{kind, path}`: `note` (its text, up to 8000 characters), `folder` (the notes in it, up to 200) or `image` (`path` is an id from `/api/assistant/uploads`). A snapshot of them is stored with the message (`meta.attach`, `meta.context`) and stays in the chat's context. Replies as server-sent events, one JSON object per `data:` line: `start {model, context}`, `ask {id, question, options: [{label, description, approve}], allow_other}` (Mnemo's `ask_owner`: the reply ends and waits for the answer), `steered {text}`, `compacting` and `compacted {messages, tokens}` (the chat was near full and its older messages were folded into a summary first), `thinking {delta}` (the model's thinking, where the provider shows it), `text {delta}`, `tool_start {id, name, args}`, `tool_end {id, name, ok, summary, ms}`, `notice {text}`, `error {message}`, `done {input_tokens, output_tokens, title, context}`. `409` while the chat is already answering. The reply runs on the server: closing the stream does not stop it (watch it again with `/live`, end it with `/stop`); `GET /api/assistant/sessions` and `GET /api/assistant/sessions/{id}` say `running` meanwhile. |
| POST | `/api/assistant/uploads?name=<file>` | The raw bytes of a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF (the Images upload limit applies): `{id, name, bytes, url}`. The image waits in `assistant-uploads/` in the state folder for a week. Attached to a chat message, it goes to the model as an image (OpenAI `image_url`, Responses `input_image`, Anthropic `image` blocks; the newest 6 images of the chat, each up to 4.5 MB; a model that refuses images gets their names instead), and Mnemo's `place_image` tool can put it beside a note through MCP `upload_image`. |
| GET | `/api/assistant/uploads/{id}` | The staged image, for the chat's thumbnails. |

Mnemo runs its tools through the MCP server under the name **Mnemo** (actor id
`mnemo`), so every call shows in Activity and respects tools switched off on the
Tools page. It has one tool of its own, `place_image {upload, note, name?, alt?,
append?}`, which hands a staged chat image to `upload_image` (and is off when
that tool is off).

Thinking: Anthropic models are asked for adaptive thinking with summaries
(models that refuse the field are asked without it from then on), OpenAI GPT-5
and o-series models on the Responses API for reasoning summaries, and
OpenAI-compatible servers stream `reasoning_content` or `reasoning` on their
own. A Claude reply that carried thinking is stored block for block
(`meta.raw`) and sent back verbatim, and each chat keeps the system prompt it
started with (`meta.system` on its first message), so the model's earlier
thinking stays valid. Thinking from before a compaction is not replayed, and
when the API refuses a replayed thinking block the request is sent again
without it. Permission (`POST /api/assistant/prefs` `{permission: "ask" | "auto"}`, default `ask`): in Ask first mode a tool call that would change notes is refused until the owner's latest message approves (an `answer` with `approve: true`, or an `@mnemo:` request from a note); Auto lets changes through and runs up to 40 steps a reply (25 otherwise; `max_steps` overrides, up to 60). Besides `place_image` it has `ask_owner` (a question with 2 to 5 options and Other), `current_time` (date, time, weekday and the owner's time zone), `search_docs` and `read_docs` (Memora's own documentation, from `mnemo-docs.json` the web build writes next to the assets; answers link `/docs/<page>#<heading>`), `show_items` (cards in the reply for notes, folders,
images or the vault; `tool_end` carries the checked items as `shown`) and two tools of its own over its chats, `search_chats`
(every word, newest first) and `read_chat` (one chat's messages), for when the owner
refers to an earlier conversation. It may use 54 tools for reading and looking after notes, folders,
tags, links, pins, history and the Trash; it never gets `delete_memory`,
`bulk_delete`, `delete_folder`, export or import, admin or web tools. A line with `@mnemo: <request>` in a note (outside code; a struck
`~~@mnemo: …~~` is done) is a request to Mnemo: a few seconds after the owner
saves the note (`POST /api/save` or `/api/create`), or after an agent's tool
call changes it, Mnemo runs it as a chat of its own (one per request, titled
`@mnemo · <note>: <request>`, scope `note:<path>`; the first message holds the
request as written, `meta.mention` says `{path, line, by}` and `meta.attach` names
the note), then saves the note with
the request struck through and its reply quoted under it. Activity events of
Mnemo's tool calls carry `for` ("owner · chat", "owner · console",
"<who> · @mnemo in <note>"). A chat keeps
its whole conversation for its model: when its history passes 80% of the tokens
it may use, the chat's model folds the older turns into a summary (stored as a
message with `meta.compact`, sent in front of the kept turns) before the next
reply, keeping the last one or two turns as they are. Only if that fails are the
oldest turns left out (a reply and its tool results always stay together).

## Status codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Success. |
| 201 | OAuth client registered. |
| 202 | MCP notification accepted. |
| 204 | `/favicon.ico`. |
| 302 | Redirect (pages to `/login` without a session, `/login` to `/` when signed in, logout to `/login`, locked instance to `/login?locked=1`, `/oauth/authorize` to the consent page). |
| 304 | Not modified (`/api/vault/file`, static assets). |
| 400 | Bad request, for example a missing required field or an invalid value. |
| 401 | Missing or invalid credentials, or a session-only endpoint called without a session. |
| 403 | Blocked by an access rule, a CSRF origin mismatch, a missing key scope, a wrong password or setup code, or an endpoint that needs an open setup or reset window. |
| 404 | Note, key, session, rule, or route not found; also any request for a host outside the domain list. |
| 405 | `/mcp` called with a method other than `POST`. |
| 408 | The request took longer than 30 seconds. |
| 409 | No vault configured (`needs_vault: true`), or a state conflict. |
| 413 | Body, layout, image, or event too large. |
| 415 | `/api/vault/file` path is not an image. |
| 423 | Instance is LOCKED. |
| 429 | Rate limit or failed-attempt cooldown (`Retry-After` header). |
| 500 | Internal error, for example the state database failed. |
| 503 | UI assets are not installed, the password hashing pool is busy, or too many realtime clients. |

title: Deployment
text:
# Deployment

This guide covers health checks, running Memora behind a reverse proxy, in a
container, and under systemd, first-run and recovery, backups, and upgrades.
For the installer and the Compose quick start, see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md);
for every setting, see [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md).

## Health check

`GET /healthz` is public, never rate limited, and reachable even while the
instance is LOCKED. An outside caller gets only:

```json
{ "ok": true, "server": "memora" }
```

A caller on the same machine (loopback) or a signed-in browser gets more
detail:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "server": "memora",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "vault_configured": true,
  "vault": "/var/lib/memora/vault",
  "armed": false,
  "locked": false,
  "base_url": "https://memory.example.com",
  "base_url_configured": true
}
```

Use it for container health checks and load balancer probes. Run locally, it
also tells you whether a setup window is open or the instance is locked.

## Reverse proxy

The `memora` binary binds `127.0.0.1` by default, which is the intended setup
behind a proxy on the same host (`install.sh --behind-proxy` does the same).
Bind `0.0.0.0` only when clients connect directly.

On the proxy:

- Forward `Host`, and append the client IP to `X-Forwarded-For`.
  Memora reads the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry that is not itself a
  trusted proxy; only when there is none does it fall back to
  `CF-Connecting-IP`, then `X-Real-IP`. Forwarding headers count only when the
  connection comes from a trusted proxy. Loopback is always trusted; list any
  other proxy address in `MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES`. A loopback address in a
  header is ignored, so no outside caller can pass as local.
- Forward `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. From a trusted proxy, it makes Memora mark
  the session cookie `Secure` and send HSTS.
- Upgrade WebSockets on `/ws` and allow long-lived connections there.

Set `MEMORA_BASE_URL` to the public URL (OAuth clients and connection snippets
use it) and, optionally, `MEMORA_DOMAIN` to refuse requests for other
hostnames.

### nginx

```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name memory.example.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8400;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location /ws {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8400;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
    }
}
```

### Caddy

```
memory.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8400
}
```

Caddy handles WebSocket upgrades and the `X-Forwarded-*` headers itself.

## Running in a container

The repository ships a `Dockerfile` and a `docker-compose.yml`;
[docker/README.md](../docker/README.md) is the short practical guide. The
essentials:

```sh
mkdir -p data state && sudo chown -R 1000:1000 data state
docker compose up -d
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8400/healthz
docker compose exec -it gateway memora-cli      # then /guide, or /web
```

The container runs as uid:gid 1000:1000 by default. Set `MEMORA_UID` and
`MEMORA_GID` in `.env` to match the owner of the host vault and state
directories. If the container cannot write to them, the entrypoint stops and
prints the container uid and the directory owner. A root-owned bind mount is
the most common startup failure.

Inside the container, the vault is `/data` and the state directory is
`/state`, bind-mounted from `MEMORA_DATA_DIR` and `MEMORA_STATE_DIR` (default
`./data` and `./state`). Port `8400` is the only port: the HTTP API, MCP, the
UI, and the WebSocket share it. `MEMORA_HTTP_PORT` sets the host side of the
mapping.

Behind a proxy on the host, publish on loopback only
(`MEMORA_HTTP_PORT=127.0.0.1:8400`). The container then sees the proxy as the
Docker network's gateway address, so add that address to
`MEMORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES`.

The entrypoint also accepts `setup`, `reset-password`, `status`, `unlock`,
`list`, and `cli <args>` as the container command, for one-off runs such as
`docker compose run --rm gateway cli db check`.

### Restricted container runtimes

Some hosts run containers inside another sandbox that does not grant full
kernel privileges. The container runtime can then fail before Memora starts,
with errors such as:

```
apparmor_parser: Access denied. You need policy admin privileges.
```

or:

```
runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init:
open sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start file: reopen fd 8: permission denied
```

These come from the runtime loading an AppArmor profile and writing network
sysctls, not from anything Memora needs. If you control the runtime, run the
container with AppArmor unconfined (when the outer sandbox already confines
it) and without the optional network sysctls, or use a wrapper runtime that
removes those fields from the OCI spec. Do not use `--privileged`: it is not
required and does not fix either cause.

## systemd

`install.sh` writes a hardened unit to `/etc/systemd/system/memora.service`;
its full contents are in [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#the-systemd-unit). Put local
changes in a drop-in (`sudo systemctl edit memora`), because the installer
rewrites the unit on every run.

For a manual install, a minimal unit looks like this:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Memora memory vault
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=memora
Group=memora
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/memora
Environment=HOME=/var/lib/memora
Environment=MEMORA_STATE=/var/lib/memora/state
Environment=MEMORA_VAULT=/var/lib/memora/vault
Environment=MEMORA_ASSETS=/usr/local/share/memora/assets
Environment=MEMORA_BIND=127.0.0.1
Environment=MEMORA_PORT=8400
Environment=RUST_LOG=info
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/memora
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
TimeoutStopSec=15
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=yes
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/memora

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Memora needs write access to the vault and the state directory, and `git` on
the `PATH` for vault history. Then:

```sh
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now memora
sudo memora-cli setup
```

Run as root, `memora-cli` finds the running server's state directory and does
its database work as the owner of that directory.

## First-run and recovery

The CLI opens a short window and the browser completes it:

```sh
memora-cli setup                 # first-run window, prints a one-time code
memora-cli reset-password        # password reset window, prints a one-time code
memora-cli setup --minutes 10    # longer window (1-60 minutes, default 5)
memora-cli status                # state dir, vault, owner, window, and lock
memora-cli disarm                # close an open window without locking
memora-cli unlock                # lift the lock; the owner account stays as it is
memora-cli list                  # the owner and the API keys
memora-cli clear-cooldowns       # clear login cooldowns in the running server
```

In the console (`memora-cli` with no arguments), `/web` does the same as
`setup` or `reset-password`, and `/guide` walks through the first run.

Then open `/login`, enter the code, and fill in the form before the window
closes. A wrong code counts against that IP's budget of 3 (then it waits 5
minutes); the code stays valid and single-use until the window ends. Only 50
wrong codes in one window, from any IPs, close it early; open a new one then. If a window expires
unfinished, the instance locks: API and MCP return `423` and pages go to the lock screen until
`setup`, `reset-password`, or `unlock` runs. This keeps an unclaimed instance
from being taken over by whoever reaches the port first.

### Failed sign-ins

Memora limits guessing without letting anyone lock you out:

- Per IP: 5 failed sign-ins (or 3 wrong setup codes) within 15 minutes put
  that IP on a cooldown of 5, then 10, then 15 minutes (`429`). A successful
  sign-in from the IP clears it.
- Across all IPs: 20 failures within 15 minutes switch on slow mode for 15
  minutes after the latest failure. Every sign-in then waits about a second,
  and one failure is enough to put an IP on its cooldown. There is no
  account-wide lockout: a correct password from an IP without recent failures
  still signs in, and that ends slow mode.
- `memora-cli clear-cooldowns` clears every cooldown in the running server.

Behind a proxy, these limits only work per client when Memora sees the real
client IP (see [Reverse proxy](#reverse-proxy)).

## Backups

Back up both the state directory and the vault.

State: one SQLite database, `memora.db`, holding the owner, API keys,
sessions, settings, access and privacy rules, OAuth grants, and the activity
log, plus `key-seal.bin`. It is small but critical: losing it means losing the
account and every API key. Back it up online with the CLI; never `cp` a live
database, because recent commits sit in `memora.db-wal`:

```sh
sudo memora-cli db backup --to /var/backups/memora-state-$(date +%F).db
sudo memora-cli db check            # exit status 1 on any problem
```

Without `--to`, backups go to `state/backups/` and the newest 10 are kept
(`--keep N`). A daily systemd timer or cron job running `memora-cli db backup`
is enough; encrypt copies that leave the host. See
[DATABASE.md](DATABASE.md#operations) for details.

Vault: the markdown notes and their git history. Copy the directory, or use
git:

```sh
git -C /var/lib/memora/vault bundle create /var/backups/memora-vault-$(date +%F).bundle --all
```

`.events.jsonl` is the event log. (`.fts.db`, the search index of older
versions, is no longer used and is removed automatically.)

With Docker Compose, both live in the host directories, so an archive taken
with the container stopped covers everything:

```sh
docker compose stop gateway
tar -czf memora-$(date +%F).tar.gz data state
docker compose start gateway
```

### Restore

Stop the service, restore the database with `memora-cli db restore FILE` (it
verifies the file and keeps the replaced database in `state/backups/`), put
back `key-seal.bin` and the vault, then start the service again.

If you restore only the vault and start with an empty state directory, Memora
has no account and expects a new first-run setup; the notes are intact.

## Upgrades

Native: `sudo /usr/local/share/memora/install.sh --upgrade` or
`sudo memora-cli update` (see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#upgrading)).

Docker: pull the new image and recreate the container:

```sh
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
```

The server migrates `memora.db` on start. Take a `memora-cli db backup` first:
a database migrated by a newer release cannot be opened by an older one.

title: Architecture

# Architecture

This document describes how Memora is put together: the crates, what each one
owns, the request path from a browser or an agent to the vault, the realtime
WebSocket fan-out, the auth model, and the storage model. Every claim here maps
to code under `crates/`.

## Crate layout

Memora is a Cargo workspace with six crates. The web UI is a TypeScript app in
`web/src`, built with Vite into `crates/http/assets`.

| Crate | Binary | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| `memora-core` | (library) | The vault: walking notes, parsing wikilinks and frontmatter, the in-memory note index, search, the graph, git versioning, per-caller path visibility, and the `*_impl` methods that every interface calls. Also the realtime event hub. |
| `memora-gateway` | (library) | Auth primitives: argon2id password hashing, API key generation and hashing, OAuth token and PKCE helpers, setup codes, the access stack evaluator, host and lock allow lists, scopes and per-key tool permissions, and reading the provisioning environment. No state of its own. |
| `memora-state` | (library) | The state database `memora.db` (SQLite, WAL): opening, migrations, change detection, and one typed repository per table group (owner, settings, `server_config`, keys, tools, usage, sessions, arm window, access rules, activity, control requests, OAuth, privacy rules, UI layouts, retention), plus the one-time import of JSON state files. No SQL lives outside this crate. |
| `memora-mcp` | (library) | The MCP server: the tool catalog, JSON-RPC 2.0 handling, the discovery card, client detection, `ai_activity` events, and the privacy view applied to agent callers. |
| `memora-http` | `memora` | The axum server: routing, middleware, the REST API, OAuth 2.1 endpoints, the privacy API, the WebSocket and intake bus, sealed key copies, and serving the UI assets. |
| `memora-cli` | `memora-cli` | The operator console (slash commands such as `/guide`, `/web`, `/keys`, `/tools`, `/sessions`, `/config`, `/backup`, `/db`, `/update`) and one-shot commands (`setup`, `reset-password`, `status`, `disarm`, `unlock`, `list`, `clear-cooldowns`, `vault`, `db ...`, `update`, `version`). It opens `memora.db` directly; run as root, it does database work as the state directory's owner. |

Dependencies point one way: `http` depends on `core`, `mcp`, `gateway`, and
`state`; `mcp` depends on `core`, `gateway`, and `state`; `cli` depends on
`gateway`, `mcp`, and `state`. `core`, `gateway`, and `state` depend on no
other Memora crate.

## What each crate owns

### memora-core

`MemoryStore` is the single point through which the vault is read and written.
Both the HTTP API and the MCP tools call its `*_impl` methods, so a change made
through the UI and one made through an agent take the same code path.

- `walk()` enumerates `.md` files under the vault root, skipping dot
  directories. Walk order is stable, so tools that depend on first-hit order
  behave deterministically.
- Parsing: wikilinks, inline tags, frontmatter tags, and frontmatter fields.
- The note index: parsed facts per note (links, tags, frontmatter, text,
  checklist items) kept in memory and checked against each file's mtime and
  size on every call, so notes changed outside Memora are seen at once. Nothing
  is stored on disk.
- `search()` blends word matching over name and body with `tag:` and `#tag`
  filters, scored by hits, name hits, phrase, and position.
- The graph: nodes are notes, links are resolved wikilinks.
- Versioning: when the vault is a git repository, vault changes are committed
  to it (`create:`, `edit:`,
  `rename:`, `move:`, `delete:`, `folder:`); history, diff, restore, and
  snapshot read from that history.
- Privacy views: while a caller's `PathView` is set, listings skip hidden
  notes, hidden paths resolve as "not found", and folder operations that would
  carry hidden items along are refused. A path hook reports renames, moves, and
  deletes so privacy rules follow the notes they protect.
- The event hub (see below).

### memora-gateway

- `hash_password` and `verify_password` use argon2id.
- `generate_key` produces `memora_live_` plus 128 random bits as hex.
  `hash_api_key` stores the SHA-256 hex of the key. `verify_key` compares in
  constant time.
- `AccessStack` evaluates ordered IP, range, CIDR, domain, and catch-all rules.
  Loopback is always allowed.
- `host_allowed` checks the `Host` against `MEMORA_DOMAIN` and the host of
  `MEMORA_BASE_URL`.
- `tool_access` combines a key's scopes (`mcp`, `read`, `write`, `admin`), its
  tool list, and the global tool switches.

### memora-state

- `Db::open` creates or opens `memora.db` (0600 in a 0700 directory), refuses
  foreign or newer-schema files, and runs migrations.
- Every write is one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction (`Db::write`), so the server
  and `memora-cli` can write concurrently without losing updates.
- Sessions are looked up per request by the SHA-256 of the cookie value;
  `last_seen` and key usage are buffered and flushed in the background.
- The arm window, the LOCKED state, and the last burned window live in one
  `arm_state` row.
- Triggers bump a per-domain revision counter. The server checks
  `PRAGMA data_version` about once a second and reloads only the caches whose
  domain changed, so CLI edits apply without a restart (except
  `server_config`, which is read at startup).
- Old rows (activity, key events, sessions, trashed keys, control requests) are
  pruned hourly.
- See [DATABASE.md](DATABASE.md) for the schema and operations.

### memora-mcp

- `catalog()` returns the full tool list. Each tool carries a name, a category,
  a description, a "when to use" note, and a JSON input schema. See
  [MCP.md](MCP.md).
- `handle()` dispatches JSON-RPC methods: `initialize`,
  `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`,
  and `resources/read`. Unknown methods return JSON-RPC error `-32601`.
- `call_tool()` dispatches to `MemoryStore` under the caller's privacy view.
- Every tool call publishes `ai_activity` start and end events.
- `discovery_card()` builds the `/.well-known/mcp.json` document.
- `detect_client()` classifies a request as MCP, web, or API from the path, the
  `mcp-session-id` header, the JSON-RPC body shape, and the user agent.

### memora-http

- `build_router()` wires every route and stacks the middleware layers listed
  below.
- `AppState` holds the shared store, the MCP server, the database handle, the
  in-memory caches (owner, keys, tools, access stack, settings, arm window),
  the rate-limit guard, the allowed domains, the asset directory, and the vault
  path.
- `oauth.rs` is an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for remote MCP clients;
  `privacy.rs` serves `/api/privacy`; `secrets.rs` seals API key copies.

### memora-cli

The CLI never asks for the owner password. It opens setup and reset windows and
prints one-time codes; credentials are always typed into the browser form.

## Request path

A request enters through `axum::serve` on the single bound address. Layers run
in this order, outermost first:

1. Security headers (`mw_security_headers`): CSP, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`,
   `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, COOP/CORP,
   `Permissions-Policy`, `Cache-Control: no-store` for API and auth responses,
   and HSTS when HTTPS is reported by a trusted proxy. Applied to every
   response, including errors produced by inner layers.
2. `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (`mw_noindex`).
3. A global concurrency limit of 1024 requests.
4. A 30 second request timeout (`408`).
5. Guard (`mw_guard`): requests for a host outside the domain allow list get a
   bare `404`. Forwarding headers from untrusted peers are dropped. The caller
   IP is resolved, only when the peer is a trusted proxy, from the right-most
   `X-Forwarded-For` entry that is not a trusted proxy, else `CF-Connecting-IP`,
   else `X-Real-IP`; a loopback address in a header is ignored. Per-IP
   token buckets apply to auth endpoints and to all traffic, and callers in a
   cooldown after failed logins or bad API keys get `429`. `/healthz` and
   direct loopback callers (no forwarding headers) are not rate limited.
6. Access stack (`mw_access`): picks up changes from `memora-cli`, then
   evaluates the caller IP and the `Host` domain against the access rules. A
   block returns `403`. `/healthz` bypasses it.
7. Auth and lock gate (`mw_auth`):
   - If the instance is LOCKED and the path is neither in the lock allow list
     nor a static asset: `/api/*` and `/mcp` return `423`; other paths redirect
     to `/login`.
   - Public paths pass: `/healthz`, `/.well-known/mcp.json`, `/tools`,
     `/login`, `/logout`, `/_bus`, `/`, `/index.html`, static assets, the OAuth
     discovery and flow endpoints, and the auth endpoints
     `/api/auth/{state,login,logout,bootstrap,reset,verify}`.
   - `/ws` needs a valid session and a same-origin request.
   - A valid session cookie (`memora_sess`) passes and is touched (sliding
     TTL); the response renews the cookie's `Max-Age` too, at most every five
     minutes per session, so an active browser keeps it. The web app pings
     `/api/auth/me` every few minutes while its tab is visible and in use.
   - Remaining `/api/*` and `/mcp` requests need an API key, read from
     `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`. The key must carry
     the scope the route needs (`mcp` for `/mcp`, `admin` for keys, tools,
     access, OAuth clients, privacy, and log settings, otherwise `read` for
     GET and `write` for changes). Usage is recorded; an unknown key is logged
     (`key_fail`) and counts toward the IP's cooldown. `/mcp` answers `401`
     with a `WWW-Authenticate` header so OAuth clients can start sign-in.
8. Vault gate (`mw_vault`): until a vault folder is configured, every route
   that needs the vault (notes, graph, logs, `/mcp`) answers
   `409 {"needs_vault": true}`.

Then the matched handler runs. Unmatched browser navigations get the app shell;
other unmatched paths get a JSON `404`.

For a browser: `GET /` without a session redirects to `/login`. After login,
the UI calls the `/api/*` endpoints. Reads go to `MemoryStore`. Writes from a
cookie session pass a same-origin check, then call `MemoryStore` `*_impl`
methods, which write the note, update the index, and commit to git.

For an agent: `POST /mcp` carries a JSON-RPC body. The handler parses it,
detects the client kind, and calls the MCP server under the key's privacy view.
A tool call dispatches to the same `MemoryStore` methods the UI uses. REST
calls with an API key run under the same privacy view. See [API.md](API.md)
and [MCP.md](MCP.md).

## Realtime WebSocket fan-out

The event hub lives in `memora-core::events` as a process-wide singleton.

- `publish()` stamps `_ts`. Persistable event types (`ai_activity` start
  events, `node_created`, `node_updated`, `node_deleted`, `node_renamed`,
  `folder_meta`, `folder_changed`, `actor_alias`, `key_color`) go into a
  40-entry replay ring and are appended to `<vault>/.events.jsonl`, which is
  trimmed by the `log_max_mb` and `log_max_days` settings.
- Events are broadcast on a Tokio broadcast channel (capacity 256); a lagging
  subscriber skips missed events instead of stalling the server.
- `GET /ws` (signed-in browser, same origin, at most 512 clients) sends a
  `hello` event with the client count, replays the ring (each event marked
  `replay: true`), then streams live events. When a client disconnects, a
  `presence` event announces the new count.
- `POST /_bus` is the local intake: it publishes a JSON object, but only from a
  loopback peer with no forwarding headers and no browser headers (`Origin`,
  `Sec-Fetch-*`), so a web page cannot post to it. Everyone else gets `403`.

The WebSocket and the intake bus share the single port. There is no second port
to open or proxy.

## Auth model

Owner login (browser): the owner posts a username and password to
`/api/auth/login`. The argon2id hash is verified, a session is created, and the
`memora_sess` cookie is set (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` when HTTPS is
reported by a trusted proxy). The session slides on activity up to
`session_ttl`, with an optional absolute cap (`session_max_age`).

API keys (agents and scripts): created from the dashboard, the API, or
`memora-cli` (`/keys`); the raw key is shown once. Only the SHA-256 hex is
stored, plus an optional encrypted copy (see [Storage model](#storage-model))
so the owner can show a dashboard-created key again after re-entering the
password. Keys carry scopes and an optional tool list.

OAuth 2.1 (remote MCP clients): discovery at
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; clients register dynamically
(`/oauth/register`), by a client metadata document URL, or manually by the
owner. The flow is authorization code with PKCE S256 only. The signed-in owner
approves the request in the browser, and `/oauth/token` issues an access token
that is an ordinary API key, plus a rotating refresh token. Revoking the key
ends the connection.

Privacy rules: the owner can hide a folder or a note from chosen agents
(`deny`) or from every agent except chosen ones (`allow_only`). Rules add up;
the signed-in owner always sees everything. Rules are managed through
`/api/privacy` and the admin MCP tools.

First-run and recovery (the arm window):

- `GET /api/auth/state` is public and reports `bootstrap` (true when no owner
  exists), `armed`, `locked`, the setup hint, and readiness checks.
- `memora-cli setup` (or `/web` in the console) arms a `bootstrap` window in
  the `arm_state` row, clearing any lock, and prints a one-time code. The
  browser submits the code and creates the owner through
  `/api/auth/bootstrap`, which works only while armed and only when no owner
  exists.
- `memora-cli reset-password` arms a `reset` window; `/api/auth/reset`
  replaces the password.
- A wrong code spends that IP's small budget (3, then a cooldown); 50 wrong
  codes in one window void it. A window that expires unfinished just closes
  (back to idle; agents and signed-in browsers keep working). LOCKED is only
  entered on purpose. While locked, only the lock allow list and static assets
  are reachable. `memora-cli unlock`, `setup`, or `reset-password` clears the lock.

Lock allow list (`LOCK_ALLOWED`): `/login`, `/logout`, `/api/auth/state`,
`/api/auth/verify`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/logout`,
`/api/auth/bootstrap`, `/api/auth/reset`, `/healthz`, `/favicon.ico`.

## Storage model

Memora keeps two directories apart on purpose.

### Vault (markdown, portable)

Chosen in the browser after the first sign-in (`MEMORA_VAULT` is the
suggestion) and stored in the `settings` table.

- One `.md` file per note. Frontmatter and inline `#tags` are both supported.
- Wikilinks use `[[Note Name]]` and resolve by name, so moving or renaming a
  note does not break links.
- `.git/` is the vault history. Changes commit automatically.
- `.events.jsonl` is the append-only event log.
- `.folders.json` stores folder color, icon, and description.
- `.locks.json` stores soft locks used for collaboration.
- `.actors.json` stores actor aliases.
- `.Trash/` holds soft-deleted notes, recoverable with `restore_trash`.

### State (credentials, operational)

Set by `MEMORA_STATE` (default `state`).

- `memora.db` is the single SQLite database for all server state: the owner
  (argon2id hash), API keys (SHA-256 hex, with a trash for restore), scopes
  and tool lists, global tool switches, OAuth clients and grants, privacy
  rules, sessions (hashed ids), the arm window and lock, access rules, instance
  settings, `server_config`, UI layouts, and the activity log. It is created
  and migrated on first start; WAL mode, mode 0600.
- `key-seal.bin` is the 32-byte master key (0600) for the sealed API key copies
  (ChaCha20-Poly1305). The database holds only ciphertext, so a copy of
  `memora.db` alone reveals no key.
- `backups/` holds `memora-cli db backup` copies.
- `legacy-json-<unix time>/` holds JSON state files found at startup, moved
  there after their one-time import.
- `internal.token` is created by the container entrypoint. Memora does not use
  it.

State changes are transactional: a crash leaves either the old or the new
state, never a mix.

title: Database
text:
# State database

Memora keeps all server state in one embedded SQLite file,
`<MEMORA_STATE>/memora.db`, managed by the `memora-state` crate. The vault
(markdown notes plus git) is separate and stays plain files.

No SQL lives outside `crates/state`. The server (`memora`) and the operator
console (`memora-cli`) both open the file directly; there is no database
server, port, or password.

## Files and permissions

| Path | Mode | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `<state>/` | 0700 | The state directory. Created if missing; its mode is tightened on open. |
| `memora.db` | 0600 | The database. |
| `memora.db-wal`, `memora.db-shm` | 0600 | WAL journal and shared memory. Part of the live database; never copy `memora.db` without them while the server runs. |
| `key-seal.bin` | 0600 | Master key for the sealed API key copies (`api_key_secret`). Not inside the database. |
| `assistant.sqlite3` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`) | 0600 | Mnemo's own small database (`memora_state::assistant`): `providers` (API keys sealed with `key-seal.bin`, a four-character hint), `models`, `prefs`, `sessions` and `messages`. Kept apart from `memora.db`, so the main schema and its migrations are unchanged and an older binary simply ignores it. |
| `backups/` | 0700 | Output of `memora-cli db backup` and the pre-restore snapshot. |
| `legacy-json-<unix time>/` | 0700 | JSON state files found at startup, moved here after their one-time import. |

The state directory must be on a local filesystem. WAL needs shared memory
and does not work on NFS or SMB; the server refuses to start when WAL cannot be
enabled.

Run as root, `memora-cli` does every database operation as the owner of the
state directory (in a child process that drops privileges), so no root-owned
`memora.db*` files appear and the server can always open them.

## Connection settings

Every connection, server and CLI, uses: `journal_mode=WAL`,
`synchronous=FULL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout`, `secure_delete=ON`
(deleted rows are zeroed), `trusted_schema=OFF`, SQLite defensive mode, and a
4 MiB `journal_size_limit`.

The file is marked with `PRAGMA application_id = 0x4D454D4F` (`MEMO`). Memora
refuses to open a file with another application id, or one whose
`user_version` is newer than the binary supports.

## Schema

Conventions: times are `INTEGER` unix seconds UTC; booleans are
`INTEGER CHECK (x IN (0,1))`; every table is `STRICT`. Constraints (CHECK,
UNIQUE, foreign keys, triggers) reject invalid data at the database level; the
Rust repositories validate first to return readable errors. The DDL is in
`crates/state/migrations/*.sql`.

### Auth and settings

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| `meta` | Key/value markers (for example the legacy import marker). |
| `owner` | The single owner account: `id` is always 1, so a second account is impossible. Lowercase username (1-32 chars of `a-z0-9._-`), argon2id password hash, display name, timestamps. |
| `settings` | One row (`id = 1`): `realm`, `session_ttl`, `session_max_age`, `min_password_len`, `log_max_mb`, `log_max_days`, `vault_path` (absolute or NULL). Ranges are listed in [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md#instance-settings-web-ui). |
| `server_config` | Server settings that override the environment. Only the ten known keys are accepted, with range checks for `MEMORA_PORT`, `MEMORA_ARM_TTL`, and `MEMORA_VAULT_AUTO`. `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `MEMORA_API_KEY` cannot be stored. |
| `arm_state` | One row: `idle`, `armed`, or `locked`, the window mode (`bootstrap` or `reset`), start time, length (30-86400 s), the SHA-256 of the one-time code, lock time, and the last burned window. Checks make an armed row without a code, or a code outside an armed window, impossible. |
| `session` | Browser sessions keyed by `sid_hash`, the SHA-256 of the cookie value (the cookie itself is never stored). Source, alias, IP, user agent, `created_at`, `last_seen`. The CLI addresses sessions by a prefix of at least 8 characters of `sid_hash`. |

### API keys and tools

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| `api_key` | `id` (`k_...`), name, SHA-256 hex `hash` (unique), display `prefix`, `enabled`, `tools_all`, `color` (`#rrggbb` or NULL), `created_at`, `deleted_at` (trash). `grace_until` is unused and always NULL. |
| `api_key_scope` | Scopes per key: `mcp`, `read`, `write`, `admin`. |
| `api_key_tool` | Allowed tools per key, only when `tools_all = 0` (a trigger enforces this and clears the list when `tools_all` is set back to 1). |
| `api_key_secret` | Optional sealed copy of a dashboard-created key: `base64url(nonce || ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext)` under `key-seal.bin`. |
| `api_key_usage` | Last use, last IP, and use count per key. Separate from `api_key` so usage flushes do not trigger a key reload. |
| `api_key_event` | Per-request key events (time, IP, tool or route, path). Used for activity views and new-IP detection. |
| `tool` | Mirror of the MCP tool catalog, synced at server start. Tools missing from the catalog are marked `retired`. |
| `tool_disabled` | Globally disabled tools (foreign key to `tool`). |

### OAuth

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| `oauth_client` | Registered clients: `client_id`, name, redirect URIs (JSON array), kind (`dcr`, `cimd`, or `manual`). |
| `oauth_code` | One-time authorization codes (SHA-256), PKCE S256 challenge, redirect URI, resource, expiry. |
| `oauth_grant` | Refresh tokens (SHA-256), one per connection, rotated on every use. Each grant points at the API key that serves as its access token and is deleted with it. |

### Access, privacy, and logs

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| `access_policy` | One row: the default action when no rule matches. |
| `access_rule` | Ordered rules (`position`): kind (`ip`, `range`, `cidr`, `domain`, `all`), value, `allow` or `block`, enabled flag, note. |
| `privacy_rule` | Hides a vault path from agents: kind `folder` (the folder and everything below it) or `node` (one note), mode `deny` (hidden from the listed keys) or `allow_only` (hidden from every key not listed). Paths are vault-relative and matched case-insensitively. |
| `privacy_rule_key` | Keys a privacy rule lists. |
| `privacy_trail` | Earlier paths of a rule after renames and moves (at most 64 per rule), used only to keep log and event lines that name the item away from hidden agents. |
| `activity` | Audit log: time, event name, IP, actor (username, key id, or `cli`), detail. |
| `control_request` | Requests from `memora-cli` to the running server for state that lives in server memory (`limiter_reset`, `reload_all`), with an acknowledgement (`done_at`, `result`). |
| `ui_layout` | One JSON document per web UI layout name (canvas positions, pinned graph positions), at most 512 KiB each. |
| `pin` | The owner's pinned notes and folders in sidebar order (`position`): kind `note` or `folder`, vault-relative path. At most 200. Renames, moves and deletes done by Memora rewrite or drop them in the same transaction. |
| `revision` | One counter per cache domain (`auth`, `keys`, `tools`, `access`, `settings`, `arm`), bumped by triggers. |

Revision triggers (one per insert, update, and delete) map tables to domains:
`owner` to `auth`; `api_key`, `api_key_scope`, `api_key_tool` to `keys`;
`tool_disabled` to `tools`; `access_policy`, `access_rule` to `access`;
`settings`, `server_config` to `settings`; `arm_state` to `arm`. Sessions,
usage, events, activity, OAuth, privacy rules, pins, and UI layouts have no revision
and are read from the database when needed.

## Concurrency and change detection

- Every write is one transaction started with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so the server
  and `memora-cli` can write at the same time without losing updates.
  `busy_timeout` makes a concurrent writer wait instead of failing.
  Multi-step changes are atomic, for example a password change also deletes the
  other sessions and writes the activity row in the same transaction.
- The server keeps caches of the owner, keys, tools, access stack, settings,
  and arm window. It checks `PRAGMA data_version` on requests and at least once
  a second; when another connection committed, it reads `revision` and reloads
  only the changed domains. Changes made with `memora-cli` therefore apply on
  the next request, without a restart. `server_config` is the exception: it is
  read at startup.
- Sessions are not cached: each request looks up `session.sid_hash`, so a
  sign-out from the CLI applies on the next request.
- Hot-path writes are buffered: session `last_seen` is flushed every 5 seconds
  and key usage every 30 seconds. Pending control requests are served every 2
  seconds. Buffers are flushed on shutdown.
- Window expiry is a conditional update (`armed` to `idle`, never `locked`), and a setup code
  is checked and consumed in the same transaction, so a code works at most
  once.

Kept in memory on purpose: rate-limit token buckets and login cooldowns (a
restart resets them; cooldown starts are still written to `activity`), the
trusted proxy list, and the caches above.

## Retention

The server prunes in small batches every hour, and `memora-cli db vacuum` runs
the same pruning:

| Data | Kept |
|---|---|
| `activity` | 365 days, at most 200,000 rows |
| `api_key_event` | 30 days, at most 100,000 rows |
| `session` | Until idle longer than `session_ttl` or older than `session_max_age` |
| Trashed `api_key` rows | 90 days after `deleted_at` (scopes, tools, usage, and events cascade) |
| `control_request` | 1 day after `done_at`; unanswered requests expire after 1 hour |

## Migrations

Migrations are SQL files embedded in the binary
(`crates/state/migrations/0001_init.sql` and onward) and tracked with
`PRAGMA user_version`. Each one runs in its own `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction
together with the version bump, so a crash leaves either the old or the new
schema, and two processes opening a fresh file apply it exactly once. The
server and `memora-cli` migrate the database when they open it. A binary
refuses a database with a newer schema; to go back to an older release,
restore the backup taken before upgrading.

| Version | File | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0001_init.sql` | Base schema and revision triggers |
| 2 | `0002_ui_layout.sql` | `ui_layout` |
| 3 | `0003_colors_logs.sql` | `api_key.color`, `settings.log_max_mb`, `settings.log_max_days` |
| 4 | `0004_oauth.sql` | `oauth_client`, `oauth_code`, `oauth_grant` |
| 5 | `0005_key_secret.sql` | `api_key_secret` |
| 6 | `0006_privacy.sql` | `privacy_rule`, `privacy_rule_key`, `privacy_trail` |
| 7 | `0007_pins.sql` | `pin` |
| 8 | `0008_windows_vault_path.sql` | `settings.vault_path` accepts Windows absolute paths (table rebuilt) |

### JSON state import

When the server starts on a state directory that holds JSON state files
(`gateway.json`, `config.json`, `memora.env`, `tools.json`,
`access_stack.json`, `sessions.json`, `arm.json`, `lock.json`,
`key-usage.json`, `activity.jsonl`, and related files), it imports them once,
in one transaction, then moves them to `legacy-json-<unix time>/`. Auth data
must be valid or nothing is imported; bad log lines are skipped and counted.
Plaintext `MEMORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `MEMORA_API_KEY` values are dropped. A
summary is written to the log and the `activity` table. On a fresh state
directory the import is a no-op.

## Operations

| Task | Command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Backup (server running) | `memora-cli db backup [--to PATH] [--keep N]` | `VACUUM INTO` a consistent copy, checked with `integrity_check`, mode 0600. Default target `state/backups/memora-<UTC time>.db`; the newest 10 there are kept (`--keep N`). `--to` takes a file or a directory. |
| Backup without memora-cli | `sqlite3 memora.db ".backup '/var/backups/memora.db'"` | Never `cp` a live WAL database: recent commits sit in `memora.db-wal`. |
| Restore | `memora-cli db restore FILE [--force]` | The server must be stopped (the CLI checks for it and for any process holding `memora.db*`; `--force` skips the check). Verifies `application_id`, schema version, `integrity_check`, and foreign keys, saves the current database to `state/backups/memora-<time>-pre-restore.db`, then replaces it and removes stale `-wal`/`-shm` files. |
| Health | `memora-cli db check` | Directory and file permissions, application id, schema version, `integrity_check`, `foreign_key_check`, file sizes, last backup age. Exit status 1 on any problem, for timers and health checks. |
| Maintenance | `memora-cli db vacuum` | Prune by retention, `PRAGMA optimize`, `VACUUM`, `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. |
| Inspect | `memora-cli db shell [--write]` | Runs `sqlite3` (must be installed), read-only unless `--write`. Writes through the shell bypass Memora's checks and the activity log. |
| Export | `memora-cli db export-json [DIR]` | Writes the database out as JSON state files (default: the state directory). |

In the console: `/backup`, and `/db` with `check`, `vacuum`, or `backup`.

In Docker, run the same commands through the container:

```sh
docker compose exec gateway memora-cli db backup     # lands in ./state/backups/
docker compose exec gateway memora-cli db check
```

For a restore, stop the service first and run the CLI in a one-off container:

```sh
docker compose stop gateway
docker compose run --rm gateway cli db restore /state/backups/memora-<time>.db
docker compose start gateway
```

A daily systemd timer or cron job running `memora-cli db backup` is enough for
most installs. Back up `key-seal.bin` with the database; without it, sealed key
copies cannot be shown again (the keys themselves keep working).

## Encryption at rest

The database is not encrypted. Every credential in it is a one-way hash
(argon2id for the owner password, SHA-256 for API keys, OAuth codes and refresh
tokens, setup codes, and session ids), and sealed key copies are encrypted
under a key stored outside the database. What remains (IPs, user agents,
activity) is low sensitivity. Use a 0700 state directory, host disk
encryption, and encrypt backups that leave the host (for example with `age` or
`gpg`).

title: Tool reference
text:
# Tool switches and per-key permissions

This page describes how Memora decides which MCP tools an agent may see and
call. Two controls combine:

- **Global tool switches** turn a tool off for every API key on the server.
- **Per-key permissions** (scopes and a tool list) limit what one key may do.

They are managed in the web UI, with `memora-cli` (`/tools` and `/keys`), over
the HTTP API, and with the MCP admin tools. All of them write the same state
database (`state/memora.db`, see [../DATABASE.md](../DATABASE.md)). Tool
switches and per-key tool lists from older installs (`state/tools.json` and the
`tools` field of keys in `gateway.json`) are imported into the database once.

## Tool catalog

The switchable catalog is `memora_mcp::catalog()`: every tool with its `name`,
`category`, `description`, when to use it, and input schema (74 tools; see
[../MCP.md](../MCP.md#tools)). At startup the server mirrors the catalog into
the `tool` table, so switches and per-key grants can refer to tools by name.
A tool that leaves the catalog is marked retired, not deleted: its switch and
grants are kept but have no effect, and they apply again if the tool returns.

The admin tools (`admin_list_tools`, `admin_set_tool`, `privacy_list`,
`privacy_set`, `privacy_clear`) are not part of the catalog. They cannot be
switched off or granted through a tool list; only the `admin` scope controls
them.

## Global tool switches

Table `tool_disabled` holds one row per switched-off tool. No row means the tool
is on. A switched-off tool is hidden from `tools/list` and refused by
`tools/call` for every caller, browser sessions included. It is still listed in
the discovery card and on the `/tools` page, marked as disabled.

Switching a tool that is already in the requested position changes nothing.
A change made by another process (for example `memora-cli` while the server
runs) reaches the server within about a second, without a restart.

## Scopes

Each key has a set of scopes (table `api_key_scope`):

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | Calling `/mcp` at all, and every read-only MCP tool. |
| `read` | `GET` and `HEAD` on the `/api/*` vault routes. |
| `write` | Mutating `/api/*` vault routes, and every MCP tool that is not read-only. |
| `admin` | Managing tools, keys, access rules, log settings, OAuth clients and privacy rules (`/api/tools`, `/api/keys`, `/api/access`, `/api/logs/settings`, `/api/oauth/clients`, `/api/privacy` and everything below them), and the MCP admin tools. |

A key created without explicit scopes gets `mcp`, `read` and `write` and every
tool. Keys that MCP clients obtain through OAuth start with the same defaults.
`admin` is never granted by default. An empty scope list on create also means
the defaults.

## Per-key tool list

Each key either may use every catalog tool (`"tools": "*"`, stored as
`api_key.tools_all = 1`, the default) or only the tools listed for it
(`"tools": ["search_memory", "read_memory"]`, stored as `tools_all = 0` plus one
`api_key_tool` row per tool). An empty list allows no catalog tools. Tool names
must be catalog tools; unknown names are refused with `unknown tool: <name>`.

The tool list does not replace scopes: a tool that changes the vault still
needs `write`, even when the list names it.

## Effective access

A key may call catalog tool T over MCP when all of these hold:

1. The key is enabled.
2. The key has the `mcp` scope.
3. T is not switched off globally.
4. The key's tool list is `"*"` or contains T.
5. T is read-only, or the key has the `write` scope.

Read-only tools are the ones listed as read-only in `crates/mcp/src/activity.rs`
(the R tools in [../MCP.md](../MCP.md#tools)). Every other catalog tool needs
`write`, including tools added later until they are marked read-only.

An admin tool may be called when the key is enabled and has both `mcp` and
`admin`. Browser sessions have full access, including the admin tools, but
global switches still apply to them.

Disabled keys are rejected before MCP runs (HTTP `401`, `invalid API key`), and
a key without `mcp` gets HTTP `403` with
`{"error":"API key lacks the 'mcp' scope","required_scope":"mcp"}`.

## How refusals look

`tools/list` returns only the tools the caller may use (plus the admin tools for
admin keys).

`tools/call` on a tool the caller may not use returns JSON-RPC error `-32003`
with one of these messages:

| Message | Cause |
|---|---|
| `tool not allowed for this API key: <name>` | The key's tool list does not include the tool, or the caller lacks `admin` for an admin tool. |
| `tool disabled on this server: <name>` | The tool is switched off globally. |
| `API key lacks the 'write' scope for tool: <name>` | The tool is not read-only and the key has no `write` scope. |

A name that is neither a catalog tool nor an admin tool is not refused with
`-32003`; the call returns a tool result with `isError: true` and
`unknown tool: <name>`.

## HTTP API

These routes need a signed-in browser session or an API key with the `admin`
scope. For browser sessions, `POST` requests must be same-origin.

| Route | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/tools` | | `{tools: [{name, category, description, enabled}]}` |
| `POST /api/tools` | `{name, enabled}` | `{ok, name, enabled}`. Unknown tool or missing `enabled`: `400`. |
| `GET /api/keys` | | `{count, keys}`. Each key includes `tools` (`"*"` or a list) and `scopes`. |
| `POST /api/keys` | `{name, tools?, scopes?, color?}` | `{ok, id, key, name, prefix, persisted, color, tools, scopes}`. The raw `key` is returned once. |
| `POST /api/keys/update` | `{id, name?, enabled?, color?, tools?, scopes?}` | `{ok, id, name, enabled, color, tools, scopes, persisted}` |

`tools` is `"*"` or an array of catalog tool names. `scopes` is an array of
`mcp`, `read`, `write` and `admin`. Fields left out stay unchanged. Unknown tool
or scope names return `400` (`unknown tool: <name>`, `unknown scope: <name>`).

## MCP admin tools

Listed only for keys with the `admin` scope:

- `admin_list_tools`: no arguments. Same shape as `GET /api/tools`.
- `admin_set_tool`: `{name, enabled}`. Same effect as `POST /api/tools`.

The privacy admin tools (`privacy_list`, `privacy_set`, `privacy_clear`) are
described in [../MCP.md](../MCP.md#admin-tools-admin).

## Activity log

Every change is written to the `activity` table in the same transaction:

| Event | When | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `tool_enabled` | A tool is switched on | The tool name |
| `tool_disabled` | A tool is switched off | The tool name |
| `key_permissions` | A key's scopes or tool list are set on create or changed on update | `<id> tools=[...] scopes=[...]` |

Creating and updating a key also logs `key_created` and `key_updated`. The actor
is the signed-in user, or `key:<id>` when an API key made the change.

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

Security fixes are applied to the latest release. Run the newest published
version to receive them.

| Version | Supported |
|---|---|
| Latest release | Yes |
| Older releases | No |

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue for a security problem. Report it privately:

- Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on the repository
  (Security tab, "Report a vulnerability"), or
- Email the maintainers at the address listed in the repository profile.

Include as much as you can:

- A description of the issue and its impact.
- Steps to reproduce, or a proof of concept.
- Affected version and deployment method (binary or container).
- Any suggested fix or mitigation.

We aim to acknowledge reports within a few business days and to provide a
timeline for a fix. We will credit reporters who wish to be named once a fix is
released.

## Security model

Memora is designed to run as a single-owner service, usually behind a reverse
proxy. Relevant properties:

- User passwords are stored as argon2id hashes and verified in constant time.
- API keys are random, shown once, and stored only as SHA-256 hex. Verification
  is constant time. Unknown hash formats are rejected.
- Browser sessions use an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie with a sliding TTL.
  Only a hash of the session id is stored. The `Secure` attribute is set when
  the request arrives over HTTPS through a trusted proxy.
- Cookie-based writes are protected by an origin check (`Origin`/`Referer`
  against `Host`). Pages are served with a nonce-based Content-Security-Policy.
- API keys carry scopes (`mcp`, `read`, `write`, `admin`) and an optional tool
  list; tools can be switched off for every key, and privacy rules hide notes or
  folders from chosen agents.
- MCP clients that use OAuth get an ordinary API key after the owner approves
  them in the browser (authorization code with PKCE S256), so the same scopes,
  revocation and activity log apply.
- An unclaimed instance is protected by the setup window: the CLI opens a
  short-lived session and the browser completes it. If the window expires
  unfinished, the instance locks and only recovery paths stay reachable.
- The access stack can restrict access by IP, range, CIDR, and domain, with
  loopback always allowed to prevent lockout.
- The local event intake (`POST /_bus`) accepts loopback only, and refuses
  requests a browser marks as its own (`Origin`, `Sec-Fetch-*`).
- Failed sign-ins are limited per IP: after 5 failures in 15 minutes that IP
  waits 5, then 10, then 15 minutes. Failures from many IPs never lock the
  owner out: 20 failures in 15 minutes across all IPs switch on a slow mode in
  which every sign-in waits about a second and a single failure puts that IP on
  its cooldown. A correct password from an IP without recent failures is still
  accepted, and a successful sign-in ends slow mode.
- A wrong setup code counts against that IP's budget of 3 wrong codes (then a
  cooldown). The code stays single-use and the window time-limited; only 50
  wrong codes in one window (from any IPs) close it early.
- Dynamic OAuth client registration is limited per IP, and registered clients
  that never complete an authorization are removed after an hour.

## Deployment guidance

- Terminate TLS at the reverse proxy and forward `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`.
- Keep the state directory private. Its database, `memora.db`, holds credential
  hashes and the activity log.
- Back up `memora.db` with `memora-cli db backup`; losing it loses the owner
  account, API keys and settings.
- Do not expose the service directly on a public interface without a proxy and
  without the access stack configured.
- Rotate API keys periodically (web UI, `memora-cli` -> `/keys`, or
  `POST /api/keys/roll`).

## Dependencies

CI checks the dependency trees for published advisories on every push and pull
request:

- `cargo audit` checks `Cargo.lock` against the RustSec advisory database. A
  vulnerability advisory fails the build; unmaintained, unsound and yanked
  notices are shown as warnings. Advisories reviewed and found not to apply
  are listed with their reason in `.cargo/audit.toml`.
- `npm audit --omit=dev` checks the web UI packages that end up in the built
  assets.

Dependabot proposes updates for Cargo, npm, GitHub Actions and the Docker base
images. GitHub Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs. These checks only cover
advisories that have been published; they do not replace a review of the code.

## Out of scope

- Misconfiguration of a reverse proxy or TLS termination.
- Issues that require an already-compromised host or root access.
- Denial of service from an attacker with unlimited network access, absent a
  specific, novel amplification vector.
